# Vehicle Identification Number

Definition of vehicle identification number (VIN) and VIN Search.

### Definition

A VIN, also known as a serial number, is a series of seventeen letters and numbers that a vehicle’s primary manufacturer assigns to each vehicle. In 1981, most vehicle manufacturers adopted this seventeen-digit standard. Since that time, no two vehicles have been assigned the same VIN.

**Note**: Alpha characters I, O and Q are not used in a VIN.

### VIN Search system

VIN Search is a system that

* can be used when a customer provides a VIN number instead of a plate number
* locates a vehicle registration number through a whole or partial VIN number (last six digits), and
* can be accessed by all staff at the Claims Contact Centre (CCC).

**Parent topic:** Estimates

# Rules on owner buy back of salvage

As a general rule, ICBC does not allow Beneficial Owners or Lessees to purchase their total loss vehicles unless there are extenuating circumstances.

### Eligibility

The policy applies to all total loss vehicles and when a Beneficial Owner or Lessee wants to keep their vehicle salvage after it has been declared a total loss by ICBC.

Note: There are subtle differences between owner buy back and owner retention. For more information, refer to Owner retention and owner buy back comparison.

text:
### Policy

ICBC does not allow Beneficial Owners or Lessees to buy back their total loss vehicles.

ICBC does not allow owner buy back for Lessees or Renters on non-owned, out of province (OOP) vehicles. In some cases ICBC may cash settle at actual cash value (ACV), less salvage value with the out of province owner.

All potential payees of the settlement proposal must be advised in advance. They must also agree to the proposal in order for the net payment amount to be enough for all insureds and lienholders. In addition, ICBC does not send copies of the settlement cheques to payees. Cheque numbers may be released, but only after at least one day from the date the cheque is issued.

Note: If there is a dispute about the settlement proposal, refer to Policy on total loss settlement disputes.

A salvage vehicle must be sold

A salvage vehicle must be sold

The applicable Estimating Services manager, or designate may permit an owner buy back on an exception-only basis under extenuating circumstances, such as but not limited to when the vehicle

* has a special value to the owner:
 + a collector vehicle
 + a vehicle with specialized equipment, or
 + a fleet operator vehicle
* poses no environmental risk or health safety risk, and
* owner acknowledges and agrees that the:
 + vehicle’s registration will be changed as appropriate, and
 + Vehicle Registration Support (VRS) Department will be informed of the required vehicle status change to Salvage or Non-repairable, and will process the change before any payment is issued by the claim office.

# Supplier trade qualification policy

Policy on trade qualification for ICBC’s suppliers’ technical positions who perform repairs on customer vehicles.

### Policy

The policy applies to the following technical positions:

* auto body collision technician
* automotive refinishing technician
* automotive refinishing prep technician
* automotive service technician
* automotive glass technician
* heavy duty equipment technician
* recreational vehicle service technician
* transport trailer technician
* motorcycle technician, and
* truck and transport mechanic.

The policy ensures that all repairs:

* are performed by qualified technicians
* meets a professional standard, and
* are in accordance to ICBC’s best practices and requirements.

Note: Trade equivalency (Supervision and Sign Off Authority) is not accepted as a trade qualification. It is strictly allowed only for the supervision of an apprentice, and does not provide certification to perform repairs on ICBC customer vehicles.

metadata.title: Supplier trade qualification policy
metadata.category: Repairs > Supplier
metadata.description: Policy on trade qualification for ICBC’s suppliers’ technical positions who perform repairs on customer vehicles.

text:
### Eligibility

The individual must provide a copy of their driver’s licence or photo identification to verify their employment, and must:

* have a valid and recognized trade qualification acquired within BC or another Canadian province, or
* be registered into an apprenticeship agreement for the specific trade they perform within the supplier facility.

 Note: Individuals, including either a certified journeyperson or someone with equivalent sign off authority, must work for the same employer that the apprentice is sponsored by, but do not have to work on-site at the same location on a full-time basis.

**Parent topic:** Supplier

# Supplier incentives and promotions policy

Policy on allowable supplier incentives and promotions

### Policy

Suppliers must not offer to provide goods or services of value to the customer on any ICBC claim, unless it is necessary to perform the work specified by ICBC.

| If the goods and services are… | They can include… |
| --- | --- |
| allowed | * cleaning of the vehicle * wiper blades, if the windshield is being replaced, and * established consumer point programs, such as Air Miles, Aeroplan. |
| not allowed | * vouchers for gasoline or food, and * additional work to the customer’s vehicle of any specific value. |

### Discounted goods or services

Any discount offered by the supplier for work that is specified by ICBC must be applied to the balance payable by ICBC and not to the amount of deductible, depreciation or taxes payable by the customer.

**Parent topic:** Supplier

# Excluded items for removing parts during refinishing

A list of the excluded items that ICBC does not pay for when removing parts during refinishing a vehicle.

### Excluded items

ICBC does not pay for the removal of the following items while refinishing a vehicle

* front windshields, and
* rear back glass (urethane set).

### Exceptions

Urethane set quarter and vent glass may be removed during refinishing when the participant supports the repair decision with photos and an explanation line entry in Mitchell Cloud Estimating (MCE) that identifies that

* paint bridging is unavoidable, and
* masking would not be acceptable.

Note: Repair facilities must consider the cost and risks involved when removing one time use encapsulated glass versus masking.

**Parent topic:** Removal of parts for refinishing

# Handle unrelated damage concern from collision repair program facility

The ICBC estimator handles concerns from a collision repair program facility regarding unrelated damage.

### When this applies

When the repair facility identifies that the vehicle has damage unrelated to the loss description taken by the Claims Contact Centre (CCC), it must document the issue and contact ICBC before beginning repairs. The ICBC estimator must

* determine if the concern is valid
* update documentation, and
* liaise with the customer.

metadata.category: Repair facilities program > Collision repair program > Manage inconsistent damage versus loss type at a collision repair facility
metadata.description: The ICBC estimator handles concerns from a collision repair program facility regarding unrelated damage.

text:
### Procedure

1. Determine if the repair facility concern is valid.

 | If damage is ... | Then ... |
 | --- | --- |
 | consistent with the reported cause of loss | * approve estimate * direct the repair facility to complete the repairs, and * the procedure ends here. |
 | not consistent with the reported cause of loss | proceed to step 2. |
2. Remove the damage on Work Center Appraisal.
3. Add in the journal notes that the damage is unrelated.
4. Call the customer to advise them of the unrelated damage.
5. Make a note in the claim on with information on the

 * unrelated damage, and
 * customer conversation.

**Parent topic:** Manage inconsistent damage versus loss type at a collision repair facility

Glass facilities who access the Glass Web Express (GWE) manage a glass claim differently when the GWE is unavailable.

# Handle a water damage claim

Steps to handle a motor vehicle water damage claim.

### Prerequisites

Customer has reported water damage to their motor vehicle.

### When this applies

Water damage can cause a number of potential problems in a vehicle, such as corrosion, mechanical and electrical problems, and mold.

Warning: Ensure you are wearing the appropriate personal protective equipment, if dealing with a potential mold issue.

metadata.title: Handle a water damage claim
metadata.category: Repairs > Light duty estimates > Water damaged vehicle policy
metadata.description: Steps to handle a motor vehicle water damage claim.

text:
### Procedure

1. Determine the likelihood of mold in the vehicle.

 | If ... | Then … |
 | --- | --- |
 | * a water or flood-damaged vehicle has had its windows and doors closed for an extended period of time, or * you suspect a potential for mold | * wear the appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) * vent the vehicle outdoors * avoid breathing the air in the vehicle, and * refer to the health and safety rules for further guidance. Caution: Personal safety is paramount. Exposure to mold and its airborne spores is a biohazard and may cause breathing issues, or trigger allergic or asthmatic conditions in some people. |
 | you have no reason to suspect mold | proceed to step 2. |
2. Look for signs of water damage in all the following locations:

 * under the hood
 * under the seats
 * under the carpets
 * under the dash, and
 * in the trunk.
3. Check that the electrical is functioning properly.
 1. Turn the ignition key to the "Accessory" position.

metadata.title: Handle a water damage claim
metadata.category: Repairs > Light duty estimates > Water damaged vehicle policy
metadata.description: Steps to handle a motor vehicle water damage claim.

text:
Warning: Do not start the vehicle.
 2. Check that the following are functioning properly:

 * accessory and warning lights and gauges
 * airbag supplemental restraint systems (SRS) warning lights, and
 * anti-lock braking system (ABS) warning lights.
4. Locate the air intake to determine potential internal engine damage.

 | If the damage ... | Then determine the likelihood of ... |
 | --- | --- |
 | was due to rising water | water ingress. |
 | has occurred when the engine was running | water being taken up through engine vacuum. |

**Parent topic:** Water damaged vehicle policy

# Full/partial vehicle decals, panel decals and vehicle wraps

Policy on full/partial vehicle decals, panel decals, and vehicle wraps under Own Damage Coverage.

### Policy

Full/partial vehicle decals, panel decals and vehicle wraps are recognized to be vehicle equipment.

ICBC provides Own Damage Coverage on full/partial vehicle decals, panel decals and vehicle wraps when they meet:

* specific conditions, and
* the definition of permanently attached equipment.

Note: The ICBC Own Damage Coverage includes indemnity on a Replacement Cost, New Vehicle Replacement Plus, or Limited Depreciation basis when the coverage has been purchased for the vehicle.

metadata.title: Full/partial vehicle decals, panel decals and vehicle wraps
metadata.category: Repairs > Light duty estimates > Estimating technical > Vehicle decals and wraps
metadata.description: Policy on full/partial vehicle decals, panel decals, and vehicle wraps under Own Damage Coverage.

text:
### Specific conditions

The conditions that must be met are

* vehicle owner or lessee must have an insurable interest in the vehicle wrap/decal
* depreciation may apply on replacement decals when the vehicle is repairable, and
* consequential damage to the surface of the vehicle must be excluded when it is caused from removal of a wrap by the use of:
 + any tool(s), and
 + application of chemical solvent, or heat.

### Permanently attached equipment

Refer to the definition of permanently attached equipment in the ICBC Autoplan Optional Policy – Division 5, Section 5.11, Coverage For Equipment.

Note: Wraps or coverings of a temporary nature that do not require a tool for removal are not covered as permanently attached equipment of a vehicle.

metadata.category: Repairs > Light duty estimates > Estimating technical > Vehicle decals and wraps

| declared value vehicle | declared value must reflect the ACV inclusive of permanently attached equipment. |

**Parent topic:** Vehicle decals and wraps

# Standards of performance for alternative parts suppliers on aftermarket parts

Guidelines for standards of performance on alternative parts supplier on aftermarket parts.

### Standards of performance

Aftermarket parts suppliers must meet the following standards of performance, and all general standards of performance:

# Alternative Transportation Service compensation

Subject to exceptions, collision repair program participants are compensated for providing customers with transportation as outlined in Alternative Transportation Service (ATS) sections of the Collision Repair Program Guide.

When the participant provides a courtesy vehicle to the customer, an hourly rate is applied as outlined below. When the participant satisfies the customer's transportation needs without providing a vehicle, a set allowance per claim is applicable.

Important: ATS compensation is not applicable if the vehicle type falls under an ATS Exclusion as described in the Collision Repair Program Guide, or when ICBC is directly paying for any alternative transportation for the customer during repairs.

When the participant satisfies the alternative transportation requirements of the customer under ATS, the following compensation applies:

Table 1. Participant provides and pays for a replacement vehicle for the customer:

| Eligible compensation | How compensation is applied |
| --- | --- |
| ATS hourly rate | Adding the total of all labour hours for * paint * repair * remove and replace * remove and reinstall, and * allowable sublet conversions then multiplying by the applicable ATS hourly rate. The total is automatically calculated and displayed on the Mitchell Cloud Estimating (MCE) estimate under "Costs". |

Table 2. Participant satisfies the customer's alternative transportation needs without providing a vehicle:

### When this applies

Tow suppliers must ensure that vehicles in their care and custody are safe and secured while in their possession.

The costs for necessary bulk materials (plastic, tape, or tarps) that are used to protect a vehicle from additional damage, such as the weather, are included in the applicable daily storage rate.

Tarps used to cover a burnt vehicle, or when requested by ICBC to be left with the vehicle can be invoiced to ICBC as follows:

* as a consumable at cost plus the applicable mark-up, and
* with a written explanation and/or photographs.

# Rules on owner retention of salvage

As a general rule, ICBC does not allow vehicle owners to retain their total loss vehicles unless there are extenuating circumstances.

### Eligibility

The policy applies to all total loss vehicles and when a customer wants to keep their vehicle salvage after it has been declared a total loss by ICBC.

Note: There are subtle differences between owner retention and owner buy back. For more information, refer to Owner retention and owner buy back comparison.

metadata.title: Rules on owner retention of salvage
metadata.category: Total losses and salvage > Salvage
metadata.description: As a general rule, ICBC does not allow vehicle owners to retain their total loss vehicles unless there are extenuating circumstances.

text:
### Policy

ICBC does not allow vehicle owners to retain their total loss vehicles.

Exception: The Estimating Services manager, or Commercial Estimating Services manager may approve exceptions for an owner retention request if there are extenuating circumstances.

ICBC does not allow owner retention for Lessees or Renters on non-owned, out of province (OOP) vehicles. In some cases ICBC may cash settle at actual cash value (ACV), less salvage value with the out of province owner.

Note: Contact the Commercial Claims MD Manager for more assistance.

All potential payees of the settlement proposal must be advised in advance. They must also agree to the proposal in order for the net payment amount to be enough for all insureds and lienholders.

Note: If there is a dispute about the settlement proposal, refer to Policy on total loss settlement disputes.

A salvage vehicle must be sold

metadata.category: Total losses and salvage > Salvage
metadata.description: As a general rule, ICBC does not allow vehicle owners to retain their total loss vehicles unless there are extenuating circumstances.

text:
Note: If there is a dispute about the settlement proposal, refer to Policy on total loss settlement disputes.

A salvage vehicle must be sold

* using the ICBC salvage procedures to ensure an appropriate recovery is completed
* with the proper designation applied and notice of the vehicle registration status given to the Vehicle Registration Support (VRS) department, and
* with consideration to any potential environmental risk for which ICBC could be held responsible.

An Estimating Services manager, Commercial Estimating Services manager, or designate may permit an owner to retain a total loss vehicle on an exception-only basis under circumstances such as, but not limited to, when the vehicle

* has a special value to the owner:
 + a collector vehicle
 + a vehicle with specialized equipment, or
 + a fleet operator vehicle
* poses no environmental risk or health safety risk, and
* owner acknowledges and agrees that the:
 + vehicle’s registration will be changed as appropriate, and
 + Vehicle Registration Support (VRS) Department will be informed of the required vehicle status change to Salvage or Non-repairable, and will process the change before any payment is issued by the claim office.

### Description

Overhaul is an operation that an estimator performs on an individual part to enable replacement or repairs on a vehicle. This includes disassembly and reassembly of the part.

# Add finish, sand, and buff labour time to an estimate

Steps to add the finish, sand, and buff labour time in Mitchell Cloud Estimating (MCE).

### When this applies

When the collision repair program participant has determined that the vehicle's pre-crash paint condition warrants the finish, sand, and buff operation.

metadata.title: Add finish, sand, and buff labour time to an estimate
metadata.category: Repairs > Refinishing > Finish, sand, and buff
metadata.description: Steps to add the finish, sand, and buff labour time in Mitchell Cloud Estimating.

text:
### Procedure

1. Take photos of the vehicle, capturing images detailing the condition of the vehicle's finish.
2. Inspect and confirm the pre-crash condition of the finish to ensure it warrants a finish, sand, and buff operation; including, that there are no previous paint flaws, such as nibs, paint chips, or runs evident.
3. Add the REQUIRES REVIEW template line from the ICBC My Templates group, in MCE, and proceed with repairs.
4. Navigate to the estimate, clicking the Parts icon in the side bar.
5. Select My Templates > 01 STANDARD.
6. Select the FINISH SAND & BUFF template line, adding it to the estimate.
7. Enter 0.3 hours per exterior refinish hour applied on the exterior panels requiring finish, sand, and buff.

metadata.title: Add finish, sand, and buff labour time to an estimate
metadata.category: Repairs > Refinishing > Finish, sand, and buff
metadata.description: Steps to add the finish, sand, and buff labour time in Mitchell Cloud Estimating.

text:
Note: For calculation, use the equation: Total exterior refinish time for panels requiring finish, sand and buff x 0.3 hours = total finish, sand, and buff time entered on estimate.
8. Replace information in the explanation line field with the calculation result, explaining which panels qualify for finish, sand, and buff.

 **Example:** 
 Example of an explanation line note: Lt Frt Door 2.5, Lft Rear Door 2 x 0.3 = 1.4

 Important: Finish, sand, and buff must not be applied when a de-nib and finesse operation is on an estimate.
9. Upload photos to Mitchell Connect supporting that 

 * the pre-existing clear coat condition is smooth with no orange peel, and
 * an applicable panel has been fully sanded prior to polishing.

# Estimate a propane- or natural gas-fuelled vehicle

Steps to estimate a propane- or natural gas-fuelled vehicle.

### When this applies

Vehicle fuelled by liquid propane gas (LPG) or compressed natural gas (CNG) pose potential fire or explosion hazards when damaged.

Estimate all LPG or CNG vehicles, driveable or non-driveable, on a priority basis.

metadata.title: Estimate a propane- or natural gas-fuelled vehicle
metadata.category: Repairs > Light duty estimates > Safety considerations
metadata.description: Steps to estimate a propane- or natural gas-fuelled vehicle.

text:
### Procedure

1. Visually check for LPG or CNG vehicles if not identified on the Estimate or Appraisal.
2. Determine whether the vehicle is driveable.

 | If the vehicle is ... | Then ... |
 | --- | --- |
 | driveable | proceed to step 7. |
 | not driveable | proceed to step 3. |
3. Place red cone on roof of vehicle.

 Note: This identifies the vehicle as fuelled by LPG or CNG.

 Exception: If it is a mobile estimate, this step is not necessary.
4. Disconnect battery cables.

 If you need to cut battery cables to do so, include their replacement on the Estimate or Appraisal.
5. Close all cylinder shut-off valves.

 Include any that are

 * enclosed in a sealed cover or bag, and
 * vented outside the vehicle.
6. Ensure ignition is in off position.

 Note: This ensures the solenoid valve remains closed.
7. Estimate the vehicle using standard estimating procedures.
8. Complete a Request Tow Activity as follows:

metadata.category: Repairs > Light duty estimates > Safety considerations
metadata.description: Steps to estimate a propane- or natural gas-fuelled vehicle.

text:
Note: This ensures the solenoid valve remains closed.
7. Estimate the vehicle using standard estimating procedures.
8. Complete a Request Tow Activity as follows:

 | If, by closing time, the estimate is ... | And the vehicle is ... | Then have the tow company ... |
 | --- | --- | --- |
 | incomplete | * not driveable, and * at an ICBC repair facility | move the vehicle outside for the night and back inside the next day. |
 | incomplete | at a claim centre | * remove the vehicle for storage in the tow company's compound overnight, and * return the vehicle to the claim centre the next day. |

9. Make a note in ClaimCenter.

# Create interim payment on total loss settlement

Steps to create an interim payment on total loss settlement.

### When this applies

In situations where the settlement amount cannot be agreed upon due to differences of opinion on the vehicle value, the vehicle settlement representative (VSR) or estimator may consider creating an interim payment.

The settlement amount will be the actual cash value (ACV) of the vehicle as determined by ICBC, less deductible if applicable.

Note: Legal actions against third parties for disputes regarding the value of vehicles cannot be initiated for claims with a date of loss of May 1, 2021 and later.

metadata.title: Create interim payment on total loss settlement
metadata.category: Total losses and salvage > Total loss settlement dispute policy
metadata.description: Steps to create an interim payment on total loss settlement.

text:
### Procedure

1. Ensure the customer has signed one of the following forms prior to advancing the payment:

 * Vehicle Ownership Transfer Agreement (CL96)
 * Owner Retention Agreement (CL96C), or
 * Commercial Claims Salvage Purchase Agreement (CL96D)
2. Explain the following to the customer: 

 * we are advancing what we feel is fair market value for the vehicle, and
 * accepting the advance payment does not prejudice any of the customer's rights under the arbitration provision of the Insurance (Vehicle) Regulation, Section 177.
3. Provide the customer with a copy of the applicable procedure and explain how the customer should proceed.

 Advise not-liable customers that

 * they have a right of action, and
 * can institute legal proceedings should they decide to do so.

### Allowance

# Safety requirements for working with burned vehicles

List of factors to reduce the risk of exposure to inhaled or absorbed contaminants from a burned vehicle.

### Potential risk

Workers Compensation Board (WCB) and ICBC requirements include options to reduce the risk of exposure to inhaled or otherwise-absorbed contaminants resulting from a burned vehicle.

Every time a vehicle is partially or totally burned, the fire produces toxic by-products. They create a potential risk to estimators and other staff working in or around the vehicle who may inhale and/or absorb the resulting dusts.

metadata.title: Safety requirements for working with burned vehicles
metadata.category: Occupational health and safety > Biohazard inspection and cleaning of a vehicle
metadata.description: List of factors to reduce the risk of exposure to inhaled or absorbed contaminants from a burned vehicle.

text:
### Factors that affect exposure risk

Here are some factors that affect exposure risk:

metadata.title: Safety requirements for working with burned vehicles
metadata.category: Occupational health and safety > Biohazard inspection and cleaning of a vehicle
metadata.description: List of factors to reduce the risk of exposure to inhaled or absorbed contaminants from a burned vehicle.

text:
| Factor | How exposure risk is reduced |
| --- | --- |
| Lag time | A longer lag time between the time of the fire and the time the vehicle is estimated, reduces the potential risk. The risk is reduced because the vehicle may be exposed to wind, rain, and/or fire extinguishing materials. These blow or wash away dust, and lower the amount or concentration of the fire residue. |
| Air circulation/towing | Air circulation blows away fire dust and odours. The higher the air circulation, such as when the vehicle is being towed, the greater the circulation and the lower the risk. |
| Time near the vehicle | Reducing the time spent in or near the vehicle reduces the risk. If the vehicle is an obvious total loss, the estimator and other staff may spend very little time in close proximity to the vehicle. This further reduces the exposure. |
| Vehicle storage | The vehicle must not be stored inside any of ICBC’s buildings. |

metadata.title: Safety requirements for working with burned vehicles
metadata.category: Occupational health and safety > Biohazard inspection and cleaning of a vehicle
metadata.description: List of factors to reduce the risk of exposure to inhaled or absorbed contaminants from a burned vehicle.

text:
| Vehicle storage | The vehicle must not be stored inside any of ICBC’s buildings. |
| Personal protective equipment | Wearing personal protective equipment reduces direct exposure to fire residues. |
| Post-work protocol | After completing the estimate and/or removing items from the vehicle, risk can be reduced through * careful removal and disposal of the dust mask and latex gloves, and * thorough hand washing. |
| Training | The Employee Wellness Department presentation shows the risks, safe work procedures, and personal protection equipment (PPE) required when working around a burned vehicle. Knowing these risks and using these procedures and PPE help reduce exposure risk. |

metadata.title: Safety requirements for working with burned vehicles
metadata.category: Occupational health and safety > Biohazard inspection and cleaning of a vehicle

# Alternative Transportation Service for vehicles deemed to be a total loss policy

Collision repair program participants follow guidelines for providing the Alternative Transportation Service (ATS) to customers whose vehicle has been deemed a total loss.

In instances where a participant provides an ATS replacement vehicle to the customer before ICBC determines the customer's vehicle to be a total loss, ICBC compensates the participant with the ATS Vehicle Reimbursement rate.

The rate is based on the date that the initial estimate was submitted, and estimates must be submitted within two business days of the ATS Responsibility Date for both driveable and non-driveable vehicles.

metadata.title: Alternative Transportation Service for vehicles deemed to be a total loss policy
metadata.category: Repair facilities program > Alternative Transportation Service
metadata.description: Collision repair program participants follow guidelines for providing the Alternative Transportation Service (ATS) to customers whose vehicle has been deemed a total loss.

text:
### Compensation for participants

ICBC compensates the participant based on when the estimate is submitted for a vehicle deemed a total loss.

If the estimate is

* submitted within the two business days of the ATS Responsibility Date, the participant is
 + compensated for the exact number of days the ATS vehicle was provided to the customer between the ATS Responsibility Date and the date that the vehicle was deemed a total loss, and
 + able to bill one additional day, if necessary to contact the customer to arrange for the return for the vehicle, or
* not submitted within the two business days of the ATS Responsibility Date, the participant is
 + compensated for the exact number of days theATS vehicle was provided between the time the estimate was submitted and the date that the vehicle was deemed a total loss, and
 + able to bill an additional day, if necessary to contact the customer to arrange the return of the vehicle.

# Crushing vehicles policy

When a vehicle is deemed a total loss due to the result of flood damage, then the vehicle is designated as non-repairable, for dismantle purposes only (DPO) or crush.

metadata.title: Crushing vehicles policy
metadata.category: Total losses and salvage > Salvage > Salvage designation policy
metadata.description: When a vehicle is deemed a total loss due to the result of flood damage, then the vehicle is designated as non-repairable, for dismantle purposes only (DPO) or crush.

text:
### Applicability

The policy applies to the following situations that result in a total loss, and the vehicle being designated as non-repairable.

| Situation | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Vehicle meets the description of flood damage | The vehicle must be designated * non-repairable * flood * dismantle purposes only (DPO), or * crush. Components of a flood damaged vehicle may not be used as donor parts for repairing or rebuilding other vehicles, unless the donor part is * determined to be unaffected by the flooding occurrence, or * cleaned and tested, to ensure no toxic hazard or contamination remains. |
| The vehicle is * contaminated by a toxic fluid and rendered unsafe due to toxic hazard, or * exposed to contaminated water such as salt water, fertilizer, sewage, or chemical or heavy particulate. | The vehicle must be * designated non-repairable * flood * sold by Salvage Operations, and * crushed. |

metadata.category: Total losses and salvage > Salvage > Salvage designation policy
metadata.description: When a vehicle is deemed a total loss due to the result of flood damage, then the vehicle is designated as non-repairable, for dismantle purposes only (DPO) or crush.

text:
### Exceptions

A vehicle may be exempt from receiving non-repairable flood status when

* none of the vehicle’s major electrical system components have been immersed in, or covered by liquid
* the vehicle has limited and basic electrical components available, due to the vehicle’s collectible, that is manufactured in 1971 or earlier, value, or
* the vehicle
 + was subjected to fresh water flooding without the presence of harmful or toxic contaminants, and
 + may be safely repaired.

Important: All exceptions must be approved by the salvage operations manager or operations estimating services manager, and documented in the customer's claim.

**Parent topic:** Salvage designation policy

# Salvage Buyer Performance Management

The performance management model is used to support salvage sales activities, monitor and manage salvage buyer and their representative's compliance with ICBC's terms and conditions, minimize potential financial risks to ICBC using appropriate review controls, and to apply a consistent dispute resolution, suspension and/or termination process.

### Buyer dispute

When there is a dispute related to the purchase of an ICBC salvage item such as a potential misrepresentation, or missing parts, the buyer must contact ICBC Salvage Services via email at [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#a5ccc6c7c6d6c4c9d3c4c2c0e5ccc6c7c68bc6cac8).

Buyers must make reasonable efforts to notify ICBC of any disputes no later than seven business days from the salvage auction sale date to ensure timely resolution.

### Buyer representatives

The buyers are responsible and liable for all actions and omissions of their representatives, who must comply with the ICBC Terms and Conditions. Representatives may include, for greater certainty, towers and/or transporters acting on the buyer's behalf, and sanctions apply equally to them.

When a buyer's representative breaches terms and conditions, ICBC reserves the right at its sole discretion, to suspend or terminate the buyer's account and prohibit the buyer from participating in future auctions of ICBC salvage items.

Due to the relationship with the tow companies hired by the buyer, the suspension process for them is not applicable. Depending on the nature and severity of the incident, and the history of the representative, sanctions should be considered, including

* a written warning letter
* a written termination letter, and
* access restriction or removal from ICBC facilities indefinitely.

# Towing Information Management (TIM)

Information regarding the Towing Information Management (TIM) application.

### Towing Information Management (TIM) application

The Tow Information Management (TIM) is a web application used by tow companies to contact ICBC for the purpose of identifying

* whether a vehicle(s) in their possession has reported an insurance claim, and

### Usage

The TIM app link and job aid are both available on the Towing (icbc.com) page. Refer to pages 3 and 4 of the job aid for key details on how tow companies interpret information in the TIM app.

For more information on when ICBC pays for towing and storage, refer to the topic, Policy on when ICBC pays for towing and storage.

There is broken glass in a vehicle from a loss that must be vacuumed.

### When this applies

Time may be warranted for vacuuming broken glass from a vehicle and removing parts for access when performed at a collision repair program facility using Mitchell Cloud Estimating (MCE).

# Handle overdue salvage payments

How to handle an overdue payment or vehicle removal, when a vehicle has been sold as salvage.

### Prerequisites

A vehicle has been sold as salvage, and the buyer did not make a reasonable effort to notify ICBC of any disruptions that affected their ability to pay for the salvage on time.

### When this applies

A payment has not been received within two business days of the award date or removal of the purchased salvage vehicle has exceeded two business days of the award date.

Note: Coordinating pick up of salvage may exceed the standard two day grace period as payments are made online and take time to process.

metadata.title: Handle overdue salvage payments
metadata.category: Total losses and salvage > Salvage > Salvage overview
metadata.description: How to handle an overdue payment or vehicle removal, when a vehicle has been sold as salvage.

text:
### Procedure

1. Determine how many days overdue the payment is.

 | If it has been ... | Then... |
 | --- | --- |
 | two to five business days since award date | apply the late pick-up fee for the applicable number of days the payment is overdue. Note: The IAA system auto generates a nightly batch email to the buyer when the account is in arrears. |
 | more than five business days since award date | * advise your supervisor Note: Your supervisor will review the Performance Management policy to determine sanctions required. * suspend the buyer * apply appropriate late storage fee for the area, and * notify IAA, if applicable. |
2. Determine if the vehicle has been picked up.

 | --- | --- |
 | within two business days of payment date | * update the buyer account to reflect the applicable number of days the pick up is overdue, and * charge late fee once the vehicle is being picked up. |
 | more than ten business days of payment date, if applicable | * advise your supervisor * contact the buyer to discuss * send warning letter via email * consider suspension, if applicable * notify IAA of suspension applied, if applicable, and * update the buyer account to reflect the applicable number of days they are overdue. |

An auto claims specialist manages a heavy equipment or commercial vehicle claim.

### When this applies

When a heavy equipment or commercial vehicle has a claim open.

Commercial vehicles include

* trucks
* vans
* buses, and
* other vehicles used by businesses for transport, delivery, or other operational needs

Heavy equipment is defined as machinery more than 8,800 kg, including

* excavators
* bulldozers, and
* other specialized equipment used in construction, agriculture, or industrial settings

text:
### Procedure

1. Review coverage.
 1. Check tractor rate class and territory confirming correct one is listed.
 2. Check trailer rate class and compatibility.
 3. Check driver's licence to confirm class validity.
2. Contact registered owner (RO) and driver.
 1. Obtain a statement regarding the loss details.
 2. Confirm the use of vehicle on the date of loss (DOL) .
 3. Confirm the residence of driver.
 4. Advise customer of loss of use coverage.
 5. Note the conversation with the customer on the claim.
3. Arrange repairs for material damage.
 1. Determine declared value.
 2. Determine if claim is made for one or multiple units. 

 Note: Each unit requires its own claim.
 3. Acquire repair facility information.
 4. Complete material damage notes on claim.
 5. Assign material damage portion to an estimator or appraiser.

# Apply the tow-in handling fee to an estimate

Collision repair program participants can submit an estimate including the tow-in handling fee in certain circumstances.

### When this applies

Participants are eligible to charge ICBC the tow-in handling fee, listed on the Collision Repair Facility Labour Rates and Material Allowances, if the

# Freight allowances for northern British Columbia (B.C.) policy

ICBC pays specific freight allowances for shipments north of Prince George. Freight to all other areas of the province; including, Prince George, is considered included in the pre-priced part listings in Mitchell Cloud Estimating (MCE).

The following are the freight allowances depending on the part.

| Part | Freight allowance |
| --- | --- |
| * Lights * Mirrors | $5.00 |
| * Condensers * Fenders * Grills * Radiators | $10.00 |
| * Bumper covers * Bumper face bars * Doors * Hoods * Step bumpers | $20.00 |

metadata.title: Freight allowances for northern British Columbia (B.C.) policy
metadata.category: Repairs > Parts
metadata.description: ICBC pays specific freight allowances for shipments north of Prince George. Freight to all other areas of the province; including, Prince George, is considered included in the pre-priced part listings in Mitchell Cloud Estimating.

text:
Important: Collision repair program participants should make their best effort to consolidate additional smaller or auxiliary parts within the allowances noted. The repair facility can add all parts that apply; however, multiple parts orders should be consolidated with participants working with the supplier to ensure parts remain cost effective. For example, a shipment containing a bumper cover, absorber, and re-bar could be a single $20 freight charge.

Participants must

* consider the net landed cost of a replacement part inclusive of any freight charges to ensure the appropriate cost-effective option is chosen, and
* select the appropriate repair estimate entry, My Templates/01 STANDARD/FREIGHT, from My Templates list in MCE when adding freight to the repair estimate.

Air freight or special delivery charges are considered when the net part pricing and claim factors make it a cost-effective claim choice.

* Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) back-order parts delays, or

Important: Repair facilities must document that they are using the most cost-effective parts by adding an explanation line in MCE describing the rationale.

# Handling equipment or parts upgrade requests on commercial tractor claims

Part(s) or equipment upgrades on commercial tractor claims are initiated by customer request only and are of no additional claim cost to ICBC. Requests are submitted to ICBC by the commercial collision repair facility and are reviewed by an estimator.

### When this applies

The customer is requesting an upgrade to their part(s), equipment or both that was damaged in a crash.

metadata.title: Handling equipment or parts upgrade requests on commercial tractor claims
metadata.category: Repairs > Commercial claims
metadata.description: Part(s) or equipment upgrades on commercial tractor claims are initiated by customer request only and are of no additional claim cost to ICBC. Requests are submitted to ICBC by the commercial collision repair facility and are reviewed by an estimator.

text:
### Process

1. **Customer**
 1. Requests an upgrade for damaged part(s), equipment or both.
2. **Commercial collision repair facility**
 1. Writes a repair estimate reflecting all claim related damage, including

 * original part(s), equipment or both that were damaged in the crash, and
 * all applicable labour operations.
 2. Enters a Journal Note in Mitchell Connect, advising ICBC of the customers request of an upgrade to part(s), equipment or both.
3. **ICBC estimator**
 1. Reviews repair estimate submission sent by the repair program participant.
 2. Determines if the customer is eligible for an upgrade.

Important: Part(s) or equipment with potential safety issues requires proof that the part(s) or equipment is replaced, prior to the cash settlement being issued to the customer. |

# Management of customer vehicle access fees charged by towing companies policy

Guidelines on customer vehicle access allowed by tow companies.

metadata.title: Management of customer vehicle access fees charged by towing companies policy
metadata.category: Non-drivable vehicles and tows > Towing > Base towing supplier requirements
metadata.description: Guidelines on customer vehicle access allowed by tow companies.

text:
### Policy

Tow companies, with an ICBC vendor number, must provide a customer reasonable access to their vehicle during normal business hours at no charge, as per the Base towing supplier requirements.

Reasonable access may be for the purpose of retrieving personal property from the vehicle, such as house keys, medicine, eye glasses, hearing aids, or groceries.

A tow company cannot withhold personal property located in a vehicle from the owner, however tow companies can bill customers for labour costs when the removal of items from the vehicle includes

* attached
 + parts, such as wheels, tires, stereo equipment, or
 + equipment, such as a roof rack, bush guard or bike rack, or
* retrieval of personal property
 + exceeding a reasonable length of time, or
 + occurring outside normal business hours.

metadata.title: Management of customer vehicle access fees charged by towing companies policy
metadata.category: Non-drivable vehicles and tows > Towing > Base towing supplier requirements
metadata.description: Guidelines on customer vehicle access allowed by tow companies.

text:
ICBC does not pay for the removal of personal property, attached parts or equipment as these charges are not covered under Basic Vehicle Damage coverage or Optional own damage coverage. These charges are subject to the lawsuit ban, and cannot be claimed under the at-fault party’s Third Party Liability (TPL) coverage when the customer has a BVDC claim.

The claims representative must

* ensure the customer understands their responsibility to
 + contact the tow company to make arrangements for the removal of belongings and/or parts and equipment, and
 + pay for these services, if they are charged by the tow company
* approve the removal of attached parts and/or equipment, when agreed to as part of the claims process, such as a Total Loss Settlement, and
* send a Notification to remove items from vehicle (WEB1170) form, notifying both the customer and the tow company of what has been approved to be removed, such as personal items.

metadata.title: Management of customer vehicle access fees charged by towing companies policy
metadata.category: Non-drivable vehicles and tows > Towing > Base towing supplier requirements
metadata.description: Guidelines on customer vehicle access allowed by tow companies.

text:
Note: Notifying the tow company on behalf of the customer is not an authorization to invoice ICBC for the service. Customers are not allowed to perform mechanical work on their vehicles, while impounded, due to liability concerns. The customer must make arrangements for the vehicle to be moved before performing work on it.

**Parent topic:** Base towing supplier requirements

# Restocking fee and non returnable parts policy

Restocking fees and payment for non-returnable parts are only considered when the vehicle is declared a total loss by ICBC after the initial estimate has been approved.

Important: ICBC does not guarantee that consideration results in payment of restocking fees or for non-returnable parts.

The collision repair participant must add the REQUIRES REVIEW long expansion repair line from the ICBC My Templates group in Mitchell Cloud Estimating (MCE) for payment consideration on any restocking fees or when billing for non-returnable parts.

Restocking or non-returnable parts must be billed at cost and match the amounts listed on the invoice. Non-returnable parts are designated as salvage. ICBC reserves the right to collect undamaged parts from the participant.

metadata.title: Restocking fee and non returnable parts policy
metadata.category: Repairs > Parts

text:
### Instances where fees and payment are not considered

Restocking fees and payment for non-returnable parts are not considered or paid when

* obvious damage on external panels and/or components that was not included on the original estimate or supplement that deems the vehicle a total loss
* parts are readily available from suppliers, not requiring a special order
* the customer is changing the repair facility, and
* parts were ordered prior to ICBC determining if the vehicle was a total loss and certain actual cash value (ACV) thresholds were exceeded on the either the participant's original estimate or the initial supplement on an ICBC estimate, including
 + 80% threshold, applicable to vehicles with a normal status
 + combined threshold amounts of 80% on multiple claim scenarios
 + 60% threshold, applicable to vehicles with a rebuilt status, or
 + 50% threshold, applicable when an NVR+ policy is in effect.

metadata.title: Restocking fee and non returnable parts policy
metadata.category: Repairs > Parts

text:
Note: If an initial estimate is approaching the relevant ACV threshold, submitting an estimate prior to ordering parts is recommended to obtain a maximum repair value and to ensure the vehicle is not a total loss. Participants must add the REQUIRES REVIEW long expansion repair line if the estimate value is below the relevant auto-approval threshold.

**Parent topic:** Parts

metadata.category: Repairs > Parts

# De-nib and finesse policy

During the refinish process, defects in the paint may occur, such as dust particles, known as nibs. A repair facility is required to document when a de-nib and finesse process is required on a panel. The repair facility must upload photos supporting evidence that sanding was applied to each panel documented on the repair estimate.

### Description

De-nib and finessing includes the removal of small, isolated dust particles, known as nibs, by sanding away the surface defect and applying a finishing glaze (polish) to restore the gloss. After refinishing any outer panel, it may be necessary to nib sand, or de-nib, any particles found within the final finish.

metadata.title: De-nib and finesse policy
metadata.category: Repairs > Refinishing
metadata.description: During the refinish process, defects in the paint may occur, such as dust particles, known as nibs. A repair facility is required to document when a de-nib and finesse process is required on a panel. The repair facility must upload photos supporting evidence that sanding was applied to each panel documented on the repair estimate.

text:
### Eligibility

ICBC may pay for this operation only when a claim related refinish operation has been completed and photos of the de-nib and finesse process has been provided.

Note: For de-nib and finesse of exterior surface areas, an allowance of .2 per base refinish hour (20%) applies, excluding overlap and clear coat. On blended panels, the allowance should apply to the full panel refinish time. De-nib and finesse does not apply to inner refinishing.

# Exotic vehicle repair rate policy

The exotic vehicle repair rate may be applied to eligible vehicle repairs, as determined by ICBC.

### Eligibility

Exotic vehicles are rare, limited-production and high-priced vehicles that may be eligible for a higher repair rate than that of a traditional vehicle repaired at a Collision Repair Program facility. Eligibility is determined by ICBC, and requires that the vehicle meet the definition of exotic vehicle to qualify for the repair rate. Refer to the Exotic Vehicle Repair Rate - Included Vehicle List for a list of vehicles that qualify for the exotic rate.

Note: If a participant identifies a vehicle not on the eligible vehicle list that they believe qualifies for the exotic vehicle repair rate, they should flag the estimate as Requires Review, with an estimate remark to "Review for exotic rate exception". ICBC determines whether the vehicle is eligible.

metadata.title: Exotic vehicle repair rate policy
metadata.category: Repairs > Specialty vehicle repairs
metadata.description: The exotic vehicle repair rate may be applied to eligible vehicle repairs, as determined by ICBC.

text:
### Applicability

For eligible vehicles, the exotic rate is applicable only to the following labour types:

* Body
* Structural aluminium
* Frame
* Mechanical
* Feather, prime and block.

It does not apply to refinish labour.

Important: Exotic rate applied to ineligible vehicles is subject to adjustment and recovery.

### Section topics

Use the menu on the left or click on the links below to explore topics.

# ICBC Database Pre-Priced Parts

Mitchell Cloud Estimating (MCE)has pre-priced parts listing allowing specific suppliers to list alternative cost effective parts options. Additionally, ICBC lists parts and pricing under a suppliers listing named "ICBC Database Pre-Priced parts".

Some examples of these parts include, but are not limited to

* steering components
* suspension components, and
* exhaust components.

Items listed under the supplier ICBC Database Pre-Priced Parts in MCE can be purchased from any supplier, provided they meet the necessary part requirements set out in Standards of performance on aftermarket parts.

Note: Supplier invoices need to have the ICBC claim number.

If a part is not available at any supplier, please refer to the Parts selection and pricing policy.

metadata.title: ICBC Database Pre-Priced Parts
metadata.category: Repairs > Parts

text:
### Pre-priced parts database

To establish the ICBC Database Pre-Priced Parts listing, ICBC uses historical paid claims to list parts pricing for cost effective alternative parts readily available and frequently used on ICBC claims. These parts have a median price based on the last 12 months sales history, and are added into Mitchell Alternative Parts Profile (MAPP) as a pre-priced part.

ICBC conducts an annual parts pricing review to ensure that ICBC Database Pre-Priced Parts pricing is aligned with market retail. If a participant requires review of a specific ICBC Database Pre-Priced Part due to pricing discrepancy with retail, they may email MD programs at [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#f0bdb4a0829f9782919d83b099939293de939f9d) .

**Parent topic:** Parts

# Advanced driver assistance systems calibrations for collision claims

The collision repair program participant may need to calibrate cameras or radar units for vehicles equipped with advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) that are involved in a collision claim.

### Policy

For a vehicle involved in a collision claim, that is equipped with ADAS, Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) procedures may require that the participant calibrate the camera or radar unit(s) as part of the repair process.

metadata.title: Advanced driver assistance systems calibrations for collision claims
metadata.category: Vehicle damage > Estimates
metadata.description: The collision repair program participant may need to calibrate cameras or radar units for vehicles equipped with advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) that are involved in a collision claim.

text:
### Calibrations

ADAS calibrations on cameras (forward and non-forward facing) and radar units can be

* completed in-house
* sublet to another collision or glass repair program participant
* vehicle auto calibration, if applicable, or
* sublet to a non-program participant, such as a dealership.

# Parts with a visible manufacturer’s logo replacement policy

ICBC is responsible for covering the cost of repairing or replacing the vehicle, and its equipment or any part of it, with material of a similar kind or quality. When determining if an aftermarket part is an appropriate replacement for parts that have a visible Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) logo, the overall aesthetic appearance of the part must be considered.

### Applicability

The decision on the type of part to use, OEM versus aftermarket, is based on the impact that the logo has to the overall aesthetic of the vehicle.

| Effect on aesthetic of vehicle | Part to use | Visual representation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Logo does not improve overall aesthetic of vehicle and is not visible unless viewing up close | Aftermarket part, when available | |
| Logo is clearly for aesthetic appearance | OEM part | |

# Transfer of parts to recycled assemblies policy

The individual components included in a recycled assembly may not match the customers vehicle options. In certain instances, it may be necessary to transfer an undamaged part from a customers damaged assembly to a recycled replacement assembly. Examples of this include glass tint and trim options such as painted versus chrome door handles, lock cylinders or mouldings.

metadata.title: Transfer of parts to recycled assemblies policy
metadata.category: Repairs > Parts

text:
### Applying removal and installation time

Mitchell labour time required for installing a recycled part is based on a new Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) part, therefore, overhaul of all the components of a recycled assembly are included in the replacement time. When a collision repair program participant removes an undamaged component from the customer’s damaged assembly to install on the recycled assembly, they are entitled to an additional 50% of Mitchell Re&I time for the part being transferred to the recycled assembly.

Note: Participants must consider this additional cost when making decisions on parts, and be able to support their decision in a quality assurance (QA) assessment, audit, or performance review.

metadata.category: Repairs > Parts

To be eligible for the additional removal and installation time, the program participant must make a manual line entry on the estimate with an explanation note related to the recycled assembly and provide photo documentation. This is not applicable if the recycled part price has been matched with like kind and quality or OEM parts.

# Masking and bagging policy

Commercial collision repair facilities may be required to mask and bag a commercial tractor unit, in preparation for refinishing operations, to prevent overspray to adjacent, undamaged panels.

In preparation for refinishing damaged panels, perimeter masking and bagging of adjacent, undamaged panels is performed on panels exceeding 36 inches in length on

* inners, and
* major cab or chassis components.

The labour time allowance of 1.0 body labour hour can be applied, once per claim, via Mitchell in the My Template line by entering: MASKING & BAGGING GREATER THAN 36 INCHES. For commercial tractors with multiple claims that are being repaired simultaneously, only one allowance applies.

Important: Parts that are removed and reinstalled from a vehicle that do not require perimeter masking are not eligible for the allowance. Perimeter masking is included

* on panels up to 36 inches, and
* in the refinish labour allowance.

# Pricing for participant sourced alternate parts policy

A repair program participant can bill at competitive retail pricing, not exceeding 75% of the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) MSRP, for alternate parts sourced outside of the pre-priced parts listed within the estimating platform.

Repair participants must meet requirements set out in Standards of performance on aftermarket parts.

These include but are not limited to parts such as, upper/lower control arms, tie end rods, O2 sensors, mufflers, and catalytic converters.

Refer to the topic, Part mark-up policy, for more information on parts.

Note: If delivery delays impact Loss of Use (LOU) and Alternative Transportation Service (ATS), potentially charging above the pricing limits is acceptable in this instance, if it is accompanied by a line remark supporting the decision.

text:

Participants can request an ICBC review of an estimate; including,

* a hit and run claim
* potential total loss
* betterment
* allowances
* cash settlements
* back ordered parts
* questionable damage
* permanently attached equipment that is approaching or exceeds $5,000, or
* to confirm or change the Type of Loss.

Multiple claims do not require an ICBC review, unless participants require additional support with overlaps. In such cases, the participant must use the Requires Review process, and notify ICBC by emailing [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#e48787d3dda48d878687ca878b89) with a description of the overlap concerns.

Note: Participants that apply their own overlaps to claims are not required to flag, Requires Review or email.

Important: Excessive, unnecessary requests for review may

* impact participant quality assurance (QA) scores, and
* trigger performance management consequences.

# Safety test drive allowance on commercial tractor unit policy

The safety test drive allowance can be applied on commercial tractor units for commercial paint and body repairs performed at commercial collision repair facilities.

### Eligibility

Commercial collision repair suppliers may be required to perform a safety test drive when a wheel alignment is performed on vehicles that have sustained damage to the

* frame that requires corrective pushing and pulling repair labour operations
* suspension, and
* steering box, including tie rod assembly, steering components and kingpins.

Important: If the damage sustained to the tractor unit does not require a wheel alignment, the supplier cannot bill for a safety test drive.

# Managing a potential total loss at a commercial collision repair program facility

A non drive commercial vehicle over 8800 kilograms (kg) that appears to be a potential total loss is managed at a commercial collision repair program facility.

### When this applies

When a non-drive commercial vehicle over 8800 kg is received at a commercial collision repair program facility, and the damage to the vehicle resembles a potential total loss.

metadata.title: Managing a potential total loss at a commercial collision repair program facility
metadata.category: Repairs > Commercial claims
metadata.description: A non drive commercial vehicle over 8800 kilograms (kg) that appears to be a potential total loss is managed at a commercial collision repair program facility.

text:
### Process

1. **Commercial collision repair participant**
 1. Retrieves and reviews the estimate assignment in Mitchell Cloud Estimating (MCE).
 2. Determines that the damages sustained by the vehicle deem it a potential total loss.
 3. Supplements COMMERCIAL REPAIR PROGRAM ENABLED estimate.
 4. Reviews loss details.
 5. Attaches damage photos and artifacts to MCE.
 6. Enters a Journal Note indicating that actual cash value (ACV) required to determine repairability for ICBC review.
 7. Contacts the ICBC estimator assigned to the file to advise of potential total loss.
 8. Sends the estimate package to ICBC for review.

metadata.title: Managing a potential total loss at a commercial collision repair program facility
metadata.category: Repairs > Commercial claims
metadata.description: A non drive commercial vehicle over 8800 kilograms (kg) that appears to be a potential total loss is managed at a commercial collision repair program facility.

text:
Note: The participant is not required to write a full estimate in circumstances where there are substantial damages, and the participant believes that the vehicle may be a total loss.
2. **ICBC estimator**
 1. Reviews photos provided by the participant.
 2. Completes the ACV to determine repairability of the vehicle.
 3. Creates a Journal Note in MCE with the maximum repair amount.
 4. Completes and approves supplement.
 5. Contacts the

 * participant to advise of the repairability of the vehicle, and
 * ICBC to arrange the tow of the vehicle if deemed a total loss.

Collision repair program participants can request a tow to another repair facility without ICBC approval when there is a repair requirement that the originating facility cannot complete or perform, including the removal of major mechanical components. # Manage a tow request for a vehicle determined to be a total loss at a collision repair program facility

Tow requests for vehicles determined to be a total loss are managed by ICBC estimators and claims support assistants.

text:

# Application of matte paint finishes

Guidelines for the application of matte paint finishes on vehicles.

metadata.title: Application of matte paint finishes
metadata.category: Repairs > Refinishing > Refinish times and guidelines
metadata.description: Guidelines for the application of matte paint finishes on vehicles.

text:
### Guideline

In order to duplicate frozen or matte paint finishes on vehicles, it may be necessary to refinish more panels than required with a standard gloss finish, which in turn will require refinishing on all additional panels on the same viewing plane due to the sheen and variance.

Note: If frozen or matte paint refinishes are not the original equipment manufacturer's (OEM), refer to the Custom refinish allowance policy.

Table 1. Common repair scenarios and what panels qualify for refinishing:

metadata.title: Application of matte paint finishes
metadata.category: Repairs > Refinishing > Refinish times and guidelines
metadata.description: Guidelines for the application of matte paint finishes on vehicles.

text:
Table 1. Common repair scenarios and what panels qualify for refinishing:

| If ... | Then ... |
| --- | --- |
| a panel on the side of the vehicle requires refinishing (such as a door, fender, and quarter panel) | refinishing the entire side of the vehicle would be permitted. |
| a panel on the horizontal surface requires refinishing (such as the hood, trunk lid, and roof) | refinishing is contained to the affected panel. No blends are permitted from these parts to adjoining panels. |
| a bumper cover, painted cladding / moulding, or hidden inner panel requires refinishing (such as a rocker cover or end panel) | refinishing is contained to the affected panel. No blends are permitted from these parts to adjoining panels. |

metadata.title: Application of matte paint finishes
metadata.category: Repairs > Refinishing > Refinish times and guidelines
metadata.description: Guidelines for the application of matte paint finishes on vehicles.

text:
Some repairs to inner areas such as door jambs may require clear coat to be extended onto exterior panels. In these instances, participants must provide supporting documentation through photos and repair procedures, when available. An explanation line must also be added to the refinish lines detailing why refinishing additional panels are required.

Paint manufacturers state that matte clear coats cannot be polished as the gloss level of the clear coat may be altered, therefore colour, sand, and buff is not applicable.

metadata.category: Repairs > Refinishing > Refinish times and guidelines
metadata.description: Guidelines for the application of matte paint finishes on vehicles.

text:
### Allowance

Repair program participants must manually select the pre-stored entry "Clear coat gloss level adjustment" from the "My Templates" list in Mitchell Cloud Estimating (MCE).

Note: For vehicles with multiple claims, the clear coat gloss level adjustment allowance is applied to the first claim only, as the operation is performed once.

text:
### Estimate and supplement submission requirements

Participants shall only submit an item to ICBC (on an estimate, supplement or otherwise) if the item is

* selectable and approved for payment in Mitchell, or
* manually entered in Mitchell, and that item is expressly and specifically authorised for payment
 + in the Collision Repair Program guide
 + on Claims Procedures site, or
 + on a case by case basis by ICBC in writing.

The value of any item that is not listed is included in the applicable labour rate. Examples of items that are included in the applicable labour rate include, but are not limited to

* administrative services
* customer service
* estimation services, and
* cleaning services.

Important: Participants must not submit an item for payment (or otherwise) that has previously been rejected by ICBC.

# Commercial labour rate application on light commercial vehicles

The application of labour rates on over-height, light commercial vehicles.

### Eligibility

To qualify for commercial labour rates, the

* vehicle's insurance policy must have a commercial vehicle rate class
* vehicle must have a declared value due to specialized equipment or service body
* vehicle size must be greater than 24 feet long by 10 feet high by 8 feet width, and
* repair facility must be accredited as a commercial heavy equipment paint and body repair facility.

Important: Collision repair program facilities who elect to facilitate these repairs and are not an accredited commercial heavy equipment paint and body repair facility, are not eligible to charge commercial labour rates. For the rates that the collision repair program facilities must adhere to, refer to Rates schedules.

# Complex tow requirements

Description of a complex tow and WorkSafeBC requirements.

### Description

A complex tow (vehicle recovery) is a recovery operation that requires measures above the standard recovery process, and can involve one or more of the following:

* use of heavy tow truck in a mountainous, deep valley and/or with narrow road geography
* assistance of an off-road heavy equipment vehicle or specialized piece of equipment, such as a crane
* use of an extension to the winch line from the line available on the tow vehicle, due to the distance of the vehicle from the roadway
* recovery of a vehicle where the location presents a hazard such as a lake, river, or ravine, or
* recovery of a vehicle carrying or containing high risk cargo, which can pose environmental or safety issues, if accidentally released.

metadata.title: Complex tow requirements
metadata.category: Non-drivable vehicles and tows > Towing
metadata.description: Description of a complex tow and WorkSafeBC requirements.

text:
### Tow company safety requirements

All tow companies must complete the Facility and Equipment Requirements for Base Towing and Towing and Recovery Plus form (CL174J). Within the CL174J, is the Towing Supplier Safety Questionnaire, which details WorkSafeBC requirements for companies looking to perform complex tows. Based on the answers provided, ICBC determines if a tow company meets the necessary requirements.

The WorkSafeBC requirements are, as follows:

* must have a health and safety program in place
* all traffic control personnel, when required, are industry certified in standardized traffic control procedures, and
* all tow operators
 + are adequately trained in the health and safety program
 + have access to a shift supervisor or emergency contact, should additional assistance be required, and
 + have appropriate safety gear such as gloves, steel toed boots, hard hats, and high visibility vests within the vehicle.

# Determine coverage for an uninsured parked vehicle

A claim owner or exposure owner determines if coverage is available for damage to an uninsured vehicle that was parked when struck by an ICBC insured vehicle. For claims with a date of loss (DOL) on May 1, 2021, or later.

### Prerequisites

The registered owner (RO) or lessee of an uninsured vehicle has reported vehicle damage to their parked vehicle, as a result of being struck by the driver of the third party vehicle that is insured by ICBC.

### When this applies

When a RO or lessee reports a claim for damage to their uninsured parked vehicle, a claim owner or exposure owner must determine if coverage is available for the parked uninsured vehicle by confirming

* location, that is, was it on-highway or off-highway, and
* responsibility.

metadata.category: Vehicle damage
metadata.description: A claim owner or exposure owner determines if coverage is available for damage to an uninsured vehicle that was parked when struck by an ICBC insured vehicle. For claims with a date of loss (DOL) on May 1, 2021, or later.

text:
### Procedure

1. Determine if the loss location was on a highway.

 Note: As per section 173 of the Insurance (Vehicle) Act, the vehicle damage lawsuit ban does not apply to a claim occurring off highway, if the crash does not involve at least two licensed and insured standard motor vehicles.

 | If the loss was ... | Then ... |
 | --- | --- |
 | on-highway | no coverage is available for the uninsured parked vehicle damage, due to the lawsuit ban. Advise the customer that no coverage is available. Procedure ends here. |
 | off-highway | coverage may be available. Proceed to step 2. |
2. Determine responsibility, and advise the customer of the results.

 Note: For additional information, refer to Responsibility assessments.

* proof that their decal was lost or destroyed due to the vehicle windshield being replaced
* proof of vehicle ownership
* a copy of the invoice showing the windshield replacement, and
* if possible, the original conversion document.

# Prepare raw plastic parts

Definition of Mitchell Estimating (ME) additional operation preparation (prep) raw plastic parts.

### Definition

The preparation of a raw plastic part is an additional operation in the ME system. Estimators select this additional operation when they use the

* Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), or
* after-market plastic parts (i.e. polypropylene), supplied in a raw, unfinished state with no primer on them.

These types of plastic parts

* have a shiny appearance and slippery feel, and
* are typically larger parts, such as
 + bumpers
 + large cladding, or
 + wheel opening flares.

Note: Prep raw plastic parts are not permitted on other plastic substrates.

metadata.title: Prepare raw plastic parts
metadata.category: Repairs > Refinishing
metadata.description: Definition of Mitchell Estimating (ME) additional operation preparation (prep) raw plastic parts.

text:
### Preparation of raw substrate

Preparation of plastic components coming from a manufacturer or supplier in a raw/unprimed state must be allowed .2 per refinish hour (20%).

This time should be entered on the Raw Substrate Prep line in Mitchell Cloud Estimating (MCE), including the following preparation operations

* detergent wash
* alcohol/plastic cleaner wash
* additional solvent wash
* application of specialized adhesion promoter, and
* the cleaning of equipment

### Restrictions

This additional operation should not be used when the

* plastic does not share similar characteristics to (i.e. polypropylene)
* part is being repaired or supplied as an exchange part, or
* new OEM or after-market part is already primed and/or painted.

metadata.category: Repairs > Refinishing

The application of 20% of the base refinish labour paint time to the part with a minimum time of 0.3 hours.

Note: Exchange part suppliers are responsible to ensure that the primer on the bumper covers meets industry standards as per the Exchange Standards of Performance.

Steps to cash settle a driveable total loss vehicle.

### Prerequisites

The estimator has confirmed the

* claim or estimate is not on hold
* loss type, such as, hit and run , and
* vehicle is not an unsafe vehicle and damage sustained is cosmetic only.

 Note: Cosmetic damage is commonly minor dents or scrapes, not structural or mechanical, and is limited solely to the outer body or interior panels of a vehicle. For example, keys, paint scratches or sheet metal hail damage.

### When this applies

A customer requests to cash settle their vehicle that was deemed a driveable total loss.

### Procedure

1. Check the claim for potential duplicate payments.

 | If there are … | Then … |
 | --- | --- |
 | potential duplicate payments | * do not process the claim, and * contact the claim owner or exposure owner to investigate the claim. Note: Proceed to step 2 once the claim owner or exposure owner confirms that any duplicate payments have been resolved. |
 | no potential duplicate payments | proceed to step 2. |
2. Confirm if the Estimate or Appraisal already exists.

| If the Estimate or Appraisal … | Then … |
 | --- | --- |
 | already exists | * create a supplement to the Estimate or Appraisal * complete the Total Loss Valuation * establish the actual cash value (ACV) * record the ACV, and * deduct the salvage value from the ACV by using the IAA Market Guide market value, or recycled vehicle program contract amount. |
 | does not already exist | * complete the vehicle’s Estimate or Appraisal * complete the Total Loss Valuation * establish the ACV * record the ACV, and * deduct the salvage value from the ACV by using the IAA Market Value Guide market value, or recycled vehicle program contract amount. |
3. Determine the appropriate cash settlement amount.

 Cash settlement amount = ACV - salvage
4. Obtain approval from the appropriate manager.

# Requirements to qualify suppliers’ storage yards and buildings

Summary of requirements suppliers must have for their storage yards and buildings prior to qualifying as an ICBC towing supplier.

The suppliers’ storage yard(s) and building(s) must:

* be safe, separate, enclosed and secured
* restrict entry of unauthorized personnel to the storage building(s)
* display permanent signage with the towing supplier’s operating name, and their customer service telephone number:
 + the telephone number must be the correct number in which the customer may gain access to their vehicle within one hour during normal business hours

* have the capacity to safely store the customer vehicle(s) for at least two to one spaces for each towing vehicle registered with ICBC (excluding motorcycles), and
* all vehicles must be parked to allow individuals to move safely between the vehicles.

# Supplier surcharges policy

ICBC suppliers must charge for repairs based on the rates and times on the Estimate or Appraisal. Surcharging or additional charges to ICBC are not allowed.

The policy applies to all ICBC suppliers where any ICBC Estimate or Appraisal form is created and authorized.

The policy ensures that ICBC customers do not pay more than is required to have their vehicle repaired, unless the customer has requested an upgrade or substitution.

### Claim requirements

| Requirement | Circumstance |

| ICBC coverage | The customer must have purchased Collision or Comprehensive coverage from ICBC. |
| Rate class | The vehicle must be insured in one of the following rate classes: * 001 * 002 * 003 * 004 * 007 * 011 * 012 * 014 * 015 |
| Type of claim | The loss must be a: * Collision claim, or * Comprehensive claim with body or paint damage or both due to: + animal impact + vandalism + theft from auto, only if the items stolen are not insured by ICBC + other comprehensive claims, including but not limited to lightning, hail, flying rocks, or + unidentified ( hit and run ). |
| Vehicle condition | The vehicle must be driveable. |
| Suspicion | The claim must not be suspicious. |
