text:
### Training and certification

**Certification of technicians**

All repair facility technical personnel working on ICBC claims must hold a British Columbia (B.C.) recognized trade qualification or be a registered apprentice in one of the following trades:

* motor vehicle body repairer (metal and paint)
* automotive painter, or
* automotive refinishing prep technician.

**Technical training**

Repair facilities are required to maintain training for technical personnel to ensure safe, proper repairs.

The technical training requirements for the collision repair program are listed on the ICBC business partner’s page.

Motor vehicle body repair technicians utilizing anchoring, pulling and electronic measuring systems must obtain up-to-date training provided by the equipment manufacturer.

metadata.title: Collision repair program requirements
metadata.category: Repair facilities program > Collision repair program
metadata.description: Here are the categories of requirements for enrollment and status maintenance in the collision repair program.

text:
Motor vehicle body repair technicians utilizing anchoring, pulling and electronic measuring systems must obtain up-to-date training provided by the equipment manufacturer.

Automotive painter and automotive refinishing prep technicians all require manufacturer approved refinishing product training that is up-to-date, and specific to the product being used at the repair facility.

**Program administrative training**

ICBC will provide collision repair program administrative training for all repair facilities. All repair facility staff who access the estimating system, including the shop owner, manager or signing officer, with some exceptions, are required to complete the program administrative training.

Repair facilities must ensure that at least one staff member who has received program administrative training is on site at all times during program hours to write and complete accurate estimates according to the collision repair program standards.

metadata.title: Collision repair program requirements
metadata.category: Repair facilities program > Collision repair program
metadata.description: Here are the categories of requirements for enrollment and status maintenance in the collision repair program.

text:
### Safe, proper repairs

Repair facilities are required to complete safe, proper repairs that are subject to a limited warranty.

Repair facilities must follow manufacturer repair procedures related to structural panel repair or replacement, supplemental restraint systems (SRS) and advanced driver assist systems (ADST).

Note: This includes, but is not limited to, reinforcement bars, and welded or bonded panels.

Prior to accepting any work the repair facility must determine whether they are capable of performing safe, proper repairs in accordance with ICBC material damage claims procedures, the ICBC collision repair program guide and manufacturer repair procedures where applicable. If a repair facility is incapable of doing so they must refuse the job.

metadata.title: Collision repair program requirements
metadata.category: Repair facilities program > Collision repair program
metadata.description: Here are the categories of requirements for enrollment and status maintenance in the collision repair program.

text:
A repair facility that circumvents ICBC procedures or manufacturer repair procedures may be referred to the Supplier Conduct Committee, which may result in suspension of program benefits or termination from the collision repair program.

When there is a conflict between ICBC policies and manufacturer repair procedures ICBC’s policies will prevail. Examples include

* repairing alloy wheels, or
* utilizing aftermarket parts.

Manufacturer position statements, including but not limited to those relating to mechanical components may require additional review between the participant and ICBC.

text:
### Repair vehicle warranty

Repair facilities must provide a written limited warranty to vehicle owners, which

* applies only as long as the customer owns the vehicle
* applies for the life of the vehicle on body and paint repairs including materials
* applies up to the period of time as specified by the parts supplier or outlined in standards of performance in the ICBC material damage claims procedures
* certifies that repairs are performed to the safe proper repair standards outlined in the collision repair program guide, and
* must contain the
 + ICBC claim number
 + name of
 - repair facility, and
 - customer, and
 + vehicle information.

# Resolution of unsatisfactory or unsafe repairs

ICBC may become involved in resolving unsatisfactory or unsafe repairs in a claim.

metadata.title: Resolution of unsatisfactory or unsafe repairs
metadata.category: Repairs > Supplier > Supplier Conduct Committee
metadata.description: ICBC may become involved in resolving unsatisfactory or unsafe repairs in a claim.

text:
### ICBC involvement

ICBC does not recommend or guarantee the work of any particular repair facility, and is not responsible for the quality of repairs performed by suppliers. When the customer or an estimator identifies unsatisfactory or unsafe repairs during a repaired vehicle inspection, ICBC may assist in resolving the issue.

Unsatisfactory and unsafe repair concerns may be brought to the Supplier Conduct Committee for further review.

ICBC estimators and the estimating services manager are involved in resolving problems related to unsatisfactory work in the following situations.

metadata.title: Resolution of unsatisfactory or unsafe repairs
metadata.category: Repairs > Supplier > Supplier Conduct Committee
metadata.description: ICBC may become involved in resolving unsatisfactory or unsafe repairs in a claim.

text:
ICBC estimators and the estimating services manager are involved in resolving problems related to unsatisfactory work in the following situations.

| Type of issue | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Failure to comply with the instructions on the Estimate or Appraisal. | ICBC is involved in the resolution. |
| Repair-related items that do not affect the roadworthiness of the vehicle. | ICBC * directs the customer back to the original repair facility, and * gives the supplier an opportunity to correct repair deficiencies to resolve the problem directly with the customer. Note: If the issue is not resolved, then the estimating services manager takes all reasonable steps to assist the customer. |
| Unsafe repairs or repairs that affect the roadworthiness of the vehicle. | ICBC is involved in the resolution. Note: The estimating services manager must be notified of all unsafe repairs. |

**Parent topic:** Supplier Conduct Committee

text:
### Prerequisites

Claim involves a commercial vehicle.

### Context

Who to obtain a cash settlement approval from for the commercial vehicle.

### Approval process

The approval process uses the cash settlement amount, and claim type to determine who will authorize the cash settlement.

**Cash settlement amount**:

Use the table to identify the level of authorization required for a cash settlement.

| Cash settlements | Authorizer |
| --- | --- |
| Under $5,000 | Appraiser |
| $5,000 to $10,000 | Appraiser manager |
| Over $10,000 | Operations manager |

**Claim type**:

In addition to the cash settlement amount, the applicable manager must also approve of a cash settlement when the claim is a:

* hit and run claim, or
* audio, visual, and communication equipment claim.

Note: All cash settlements must meet the requirements outlined in the claim procedures.

# Tire advance disposal fees and tread codes

Definition of tire advance disposal fees and tread codes.

The tire advance disposal fees (ADF) is a fee collected on new tire sales and reinforced by the Tire Stewardship British Columbia Association (TSBC). The TSBC operates and manages the provincial scrap tire recycling program.

### Exclusions from the ADF

The recycling regulation excludes tire types that are

* used for cycles, wheelchairs, or three wheeled motorized devices designed for the transportation of people with physical disabilities
* used for aircraft or wheelbarrow
* retail value of less than $30.00
* recapped and re-trend tires, and
* tread codes for C, E, G.L, or IND.

| Tread code letters | Definitions |
| --- | --- |
| C | Compactor |
| E | Earth moving |
| G | Grader |
| L | Loader |
| IND | Industrial |

metadata.title: Tire advance disposal fees and tread codes
metadata.category: Repairs > Light duty estimates > Estimating technical > Wheels, Tires and Alignment
metadata.description: Definition of tire advance disposal fees and tread codes.

text:
### Tread codes

Tread codes are referred to as

* grader/loader,
* small-off the road, or
* industrial tires.

| Tread codes | Definitions |
| --- | --- |
| Small off the road tires | * Tires of truck type construction for off road applications without Department of Transportation (DOT) approval, and * conventional sizes smaller than 16 inches cross section and wide base sizes smaller than 20.5 inches cross section. |
| Large off the road tires | * Tires of truck type construction for off road applications without DOT approval, and * conventional sizes 16 inches and greater cross section, and wide base sizes of 20.5 inches and greater cross section. |
| Industrial tires | Identified with a sidewall marking of IND. |

text:
### Freight and crating charges

All recycled parts must include any freight or handing charges listed on the recycled parts locater. When the part is received by the collision repair program facility, the supplier invoice may have the freight and crating charges listed as a separate charge line on the invoice, however the invoice price must match what was listed on the locater.

In the event that the charges are listed on separate charge lines on the supplier invoice, ensure the part price is adjusted on the estimate to reflect the invoice part price. Add any freight or crating charges to the estimate using the "freight" line from "My template/01 Standard" in Mitchell Cloud Estimating (MCE).

Note: The part price and additional charges detailed on the supplier invoice cannot exceed the original inventoried part price from the Car-Part inventory.

# Handle a billing discrepancy

Steps on handling a billing discrepancy.

### When this applies

When a request for payment contains:

* a discrepancy between the Estimate or Appraisal and the work done or parts supplied, and
* a discrepancy that may be intentional.

metadata.title: Handle a billing discrepancy
metadata.category: Repairs > Supplier > Supplier invoice discrepancies policy
metadata.description: Steps on handling a billing discrepancy.

text:
### Procedure

1. ICBC representative
 1. Refers the case to the Manager Estimating Services.
2. Manager Estimating Services
 1. Reviews the case.

 | When ... | Then the Manager Estimating Services ... |
 | --- | --- |
 | repairs have been completed satisfactorily and there appears to be no intent to mislead ICBC or the customer | * discusses the issue with the customer and the supplier, and * agrees to a revised repair invoice. Note: The process ends here. |
 | repairs are not acceptable | instructs the supplier to complete all repairs, as contained on theEstimate or Appraisal. |
3. Supplier
 1. Completes repairs according to the Estimate or Appraisal.

 Note: The supplier will not be paid until the vehicle has been properly repaired. The supplier will also be responsible for any alternate transportation required by the customer.
4. Manager Estimating Services
 1. Places the supplier on notice (both verbally and in writing).

metadata.title: Handle a billing discrepancy
metadata.category: Repairs > Supplier > Supplier invoice discrepancies policy
metadata.description: Steps on handling a billing discrepancy.

text:
The notice states that if there is failure to abide by the terms and conditions of the Estimate or Appraisal in the future, it may result in:

 * immediate termination of their supplier number, or
 * such other sanction deemed appropriate by the Supplier Conduct Committee.

**Parent topic:** Supplier invoice discrepancies policy

# Repair estimate two year limitation period

Collision and glass repair program participants follow these guidelines for claims that are close to the two year limitation period from the date of loss (DOL).

### Limitation period

ICBC claims are subject to a two year limitation period from the DOL. Participants must know what to do when presented with a claim that is close to or beyond the end of that period.

metadata.title: Repair estimate two year limitation period
metadata.category: Vehicle damage > Estimates
metadata.description: Collision and glass repair program participants follow these guidelines for claims that are close to the two year limitation period from the date of loss (DOL).

text:
### Claims close to the limit

When a customer presents a repair facility with a claim that is nearing, or beyond, the end of the two year limitation period, the following applies.

metadata.title: Repair estimate two year limitation period
metadata.category: Vehicle damage > Estimates
metadata.description: Collision and glass repair program participants follow these guidelines for claims that are close to the two year limitation period from the date of loss (DOL).

text:
| Time period | Participant | ICBC |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sufficient time remains within the two year limitation period, for the participant to * complete all repairs, and * submit the estimate for payment. | Completes the repairs. | Handles this claim as usual. |
| It is uncertain whether the participant can complete the repairs and submit the estimate within the two year limitation period. | Contacts a claims manager or operations manager for collision claims or Provincial Glass Operations (PGO) for glass only claims for instructions. | Claims or operations manager or PGO reviews the claim details and determines whether repairs can be completed, and notes the claim accordingly. Note: * The manager may provide an extension, up to 30 days. * If participant fails to contact ICBC estimating or PGO, an estimate or invoice submitted for payment after the two year limitation period is reviewed for potential non-payment. |

# Unsafe vehicle

Definition of an unsafe vehicle (also known as, an out of service vehicle).

### Definition

An unsafe vehicle is a hazard on BC’s roads, and deemed unsafe for many reasons.

On inspection, an unsafe vehicle is not safe to use due to:

* a pre-existing mechanical condition
* wear and tear, and/or
* prior body repair work.

### Additional reading

Refer to procedure, Unsafe vehicle classifications and criteria, for a list of the unsafe group classifications, and the criteria used to deem a vehicle unsafe.

When a financial professional is assigned to a claim, claims specialists or adjusters need to:

# Water damaged vehicle policy

Water damage claims must be handled as soon as possible.

### Applicability

The procedures for handling water and flood damaged motor vehicle claims must be consistent with

* all federal and provincial laws, and
* the Canadian Council of Motor Transport Administrators (CCMTA) Guidelines.

### Rationale

Water damage escalates with time making rapid intervention important.

Water and flood damage claims present challenges with repairs due to the potential for recurring issues, particularly in the case of contaminated fluid or flood damage. These challenges include

* electrical problems
* odour
* corrosion, and/or
* health and safety concerns.

# Recycled parts trim time policy

Policy on recycled parts trim time.

### Policy

The estimator must apply a labour time to separate the recycled part from other welded components.

A judgment allowance

* is applied on all welded-on recycled parts for the trim time, and
* must be listed separate from the remove and replace(RE & RE) time on the Estimate or Appraisal.

If a recycled quarter panel is purchased as part of the repair on the vehicle, the estimator must apply a judgment time (allow extra time, at the estimator’s discretion) to the recycled part. This allows the repair facility to remove only the part(s) necessary to complete the repair.

metadata.title: Recycled parts trim time policy
metadata.category: Repairs > Parts > Recycled parts requirements
metadata.description: Policy on recycled parts trim time.

text:
### Example

The recycler cuts the whole quarter section off the vehicle and sends it to the repair facility. The repair facility needs only the outer panel. The estimator would allow time to remove the outer panel from the section. That time is above the RE & RE time required for the shop to put the panel on the vehicle. The entry must be entered on a separate line.

**Parent topic:** Recycled parts requirements

# Refinish blend

Definition of a refinish blend.

### Definition

A refinish blend is the application of colour to a portion of a vehicle panel that is adjacent to a damaged vehicle panel, when the damaged vehicle panel does not have enough undamaged surface area to facilitate a colour match.

An additional blend into the next adjacent panel is considered when the adjacent panel is less than 12 inches wide. Refinish blends are allowed on an exception basis to ensure accurate colour matching.

**Example**: If a truck cab corner measures 8 inches wide, an additional blend into the next adjoining panel may be warranted.

### Agreement of a difficult colour match

If the ICBC estimator and the repair facility manager are unable to agree on what is considered a difficult colour match, the Manager Estimating Services at the local servicing ICBC claims office makes the final decision.

Note: For further information, refer to the topic, Refinish blend allowances.

# Supplement

Definition of a supplement.

### Definition

A supplement is a change or addition made to the Estimate or Appraisal after it has been created by an ICBC estimator.

Example

The original Estimate or Appraisal requires that an A00 Suffix Identification (ID) be created. After the Estimate or Appraisal has been created, a change that is made to this is known as a supplement and modifies the Suffix ID from A00 to A01.

Supplements occurring during estimates are a result of, but not limited to:

* damage to a vehicle part
* a price correction
* refinish time
* labour time, and/or
* labour rate.

Note: Every reasonable effort must be made by the repair facility to identify all visible damage to the vehicle, including paint, on the initial supplement. Any subsequent supplement must be made for hidden damages only.

# Apply deductible when cash settling a claim

Steps to apply the deductible when cash settling a claim.

### When this applies

An estimator may choose to cash settle a claim. Claims may be settled by cash payment to the customer. Deductibles are applied according to how settlement will happen.

### Procedure

1. Complete the Estimate or Appraisal.
2. Issue payment with the deductible applied when the customer is cash settling on the entire vehicle damage.
3. Apply the deductible to the Estimate or Appraisal when a portion of the customer's vehicle repairs are completed prior to the cash settlement cheque is issued.

Tow truck equipment that is included under the tow truck’s Own Damage coverage:

* a fire extinguisher
* a flashlight
* a first aid kit, and

The mechanical rates apply when repairing the:

* engine

* clutch
* flywheel, and

* completing a separate suffix Estimate or Appraisal that describes the part covered by the mechanical rate, or

# Alternative Transportation Service

Alternative Transportation Service (ATS) is a mandatory requirement of the collision repair program.

ATS is a service offered by the collision repair program participant to customers, which

* applies to all claims regardless of the cause of loss, subject to ATS exceptions
* covers the period from the ATS responsibility date until vehicle repairs are complete, and
* satisfies the alternative transportation requirements of customers with an authorized estimate.

For further information, refer to section 9, Alternative Transportation Service and Rental, of the Collision Repair program guide.

# Disconnect a motorcycle battery

Steps to disconnect a motorcycle battery.

### Prerequisites

Before disconnecting a battery

* the following tools are required:
 + wrench, and
 + wire battery terminal brush, and
* the following safety equipment must be worn:

 + safety goggles
 + long-sleeved rubber gloves or work gloves
 + safety footwear, and
 + long pants.

Refer to the Health and wellbeing resources and Safety at work procedures for additional information.

### When this applies

Batteries must be disconnected whenever there is the potential for a battery to cause a fire or explosion.

You have determined it is safe to disconnect the battery, and you are able to do so. Follow the vehicle manufacturer’s recommended disconnection procedures if available, or these steps, even if the battery has no charge.

metadata.title: Disconnect a motorcycle battery
metadata.category: Repairs > Light duty estimates > Safety considerations
metadata.description: Steps to disconnect a motorcycle battery.

text:
### Procedure

1. Ensure it is safe to disconnect the battery(ies).
2. Locate the battery. 

 Note: A common location is directly under the seat. Remove the seat and side cover to access it.
3. Identify the positive and negative terminals. 

 | If the terminal says... | Or shows this symbol... | Then the terminal is... |
 | --- | --- | --- |
 | POS | + | positive. |
 | NEG | - | negative. |
4. Inspect the battery for a green and white ashy substance (signs of corrosion) on and around the terminals and wires.

 | If the battery … | Then ... |
 | --- | --- |
 | shows signs of corrosion | use a wire brush to remove the corrosive matter. |
 | does not show signs of corrosion | proceed to step 5. |
5. Use the correctly sized wrench to loosen the nut at the side of the negative terminal. When the nut is loose, twist the terminal off the negative post.

metadata.title: Disconnect a motorcycle battery
metadata.category: Repairs > Light duty estimates > Safety considerations
metadata.description: Steps to disconnect a motorcycle battery.

text:
Important: Always disconnect the ground (negative (-) usually black) cable from the battery first. The negative terminal is the main power link, so disconnecting it cuts off power to the motorcycle.
6. Remove the positive terminal from the positive post, if necessary. 

 | If the battery... | Then... |
 | --- | --- |
 | is being removed from the motorcycle. | disconnect the positive terminal from the battery. |
 | is not being removed from the motorcycle. | leave the positive terminal in place. |

 Note: The positive terminal is usually red.
7. Ensure the cable(s) cannot come into contact with the battery terminal or any part of the vehicle.
8. Use a yellow oil marker to mark the motorcycle B/D to indicate that the battery has been disconnected.

 Mark

 * the windshield, or
 * the gas tank.

**Parent topic:** Safety considerations

metadata.title: Disconnect a motorcycle battery
metadata.category: Repairs > Light duty estimates > Safety considerations
metadata.description: Steps to disconnect a motorcycle battery.

# Repairs of load-bearing components and structures policy

Policy on repairs of load-bearing components and structures.

### Eligibility

The policy applies to vehicles and machinery that:

* are constructed to be load-bearing (such as a crane or forklift), or
* have load-bearing equipment attached to them (such as a rollover cage attached to a tractor).

### Policy Detail

When a structural load-bearing component, designed to resist defined loads, is damaged by direct physical damage, the repair must be tested and re-certified by one of the following:

* a professional engineer, or
* original equipment manufacturer.

Important: When a claim involves such a situation, the ICBC representative must contact the exposure owner, as they provide instruction or, in certain situations, take over handling the claim.

# Biohazard inspection and cleaning of a vehicle

Circumstances when biohazard inspection and cleaning is required.

### Circumstances

The majority of recovered total thefts and vehicles that are severely damaged or exposed to contaminated or bodily fluids pose a risk to ICBC staff, customers, and business partners. These vehicles may contain biohazardous materials that are undesirable and potentially dangerous.

Whenever possible, the inspection or cleaning service must be completed prior to the insured viewing the vehicle. The following circumstances would indicate the need for a biohazard inspection and cleaning:

* recovered total theft, or
 + exposure to
* contaminated water
* bodily fluids (blood, feces, semen etc.), or
* drugs and related paraphernalia (needles, pipes, etc.).

Note: The biohazard cleaning of a vehicle is not impacted when there is a vehicle estimate hold; however, vehicles with an Special Investigation Unit (SIU) related hold should not be cleaned.

metadata.title: Biohazard inspection and cleaning of a vehicle
metadata.category: Occupational health and safety
metadata.description: Circumstances when biohazard inspection and cleaning is required.

text:
### Cleaning service provider

A qualified service provider must perform a thorough inspection and cleaning of the vehicle. The service provider must advise ICBC staff of the results of the inspection and whether cleaning

* can be restricted to the area where the hazards were found, or
* should be extended to include the entire interior and/or exterior of the vehicle.

### Benefits

The benefits of inspecting these vehicles for hazards and cleaning the vehicle include the following:

* reduced exposure by staff, customers and business partners to biohazardous materials
* an increase in customer confidence and an improved experience
* reduced liability to the Corporation, and
* claims cost control.

Recycled parts suppliers are not responsible for failure of the part during the warranty period when there is:

* improper installation
* accident
* misuses
* abuse, or

When failures to the part occurs to radiators or air conditioning parts within the applicable warranty period, the recycled parts suppliers:

* replaces the part, or

### Recycled parts for commercial vehicles

Warranty on recycled drive train components are sparse and may not be the best option for the owner. They may cause problems for the Commercial Claims Appraiser, should one fail shortly after install. Usually these parts are utilized to save on depreciation costs.

It's helpful to ensure that the owner is fully aware of the possibility of recycled parts failure and that if so, costs will be the responsibility of the owner.

A common request is to install a recycled radiator or charge air cooler, to save on depreciation. As with drive train components, the owner must fully understand the ramifications should they choose this option and the part fails. Good notes on the claim are paramount in this scenario.

Note: If a major component is to be replaced with a recycled part, confirm with the Commercial Claims MD Manager before completing the transaction. Engines fit into this category and have certain difficulties that may present.

# Handle a Garnishee Order

Steps for how an ICBC facility must handle a Garnishee Order issued by the courts and served on ICBC.

### Prerequisites

The court issued Garnishing Order names ICBC as the garnishee. ICBC has been served because ICBC owes money to an ICBC vendor or customer, and they owe money to another party or creditor.

Note: A Garnishment is a legal process that allows creditors to collect debts owed by debtors, by seizing funds owed to them. In the case of ICBC, funds owed to a vendor or customer can be items such as vendor payments, refunds, expense reimbursements, or benefits compensation.

metadata.title: Handle a Garnishee Order
metadata.category: Repairs > Supplier
metadata.description: Steps for how an ICBC facility must handle a Garnishee Order issued by the courts and served on ICBC.

text:
### When this applies

ICBC has received a Garnishee Order that requires ICBC to withhold a specific amount of money from an ICBC vendor or customer's compensation for payment to the court. The Garnishee Order is a legal document and is considered binding on ICBC.

Important: A Garnishee Order must be handled immediately to ensure that ICBC is not put at risk of having to pay the damages due to a lack of response on ICBC's part. A Garnishee Order is not to be confused as being a Notice of Civil Claim (NOCC), and is not handled as a NOCC.

### Prerequisites

The repair facility has a vehicle where the

* estimate total repair cost is close to or marginally exceeds the maximum repair cost of the vehicle

* safety of the repaired vehicle will not be compromised, and
* repair amount paid by ICBC is the only contribution to the repair cost.

### When this applies

### Procedure

 | If the ACV is … | Then the total maximum allowable repair amount must not exceed the … |
 | --- | --- |
 | $2,500 or less, including taxes | ACV. |
 | over $2,500, including taxes | maximum repair cost. |
2. Establish the maximum allowable repair amount.

# Handle and dispose of biohazardous materials

Steps to handle and dispose of biohazardous materials in a vehicle.

### When this applies

When biohazardous materials, such as syringes or needles, are found in a vehicle by an ICBC representative.

metadata.title: Handle and dispose of biohazardous materials
metadata.category: Occupational health and safety > Biohazard inspection and cleaning of a vehicle
metadata.description: Steps to handle and dispose of biohazardous materials in a vehicle.

text:
### Procedure

1. Determine whether a qualified service provider is required to remove the object.

 | If... | Then... |
 | --- | --- |
 | there is evidence of syringes or needles embedded in the vehicle trim or upholstery | * use the services of a qualified service provider, and * proceed no further with this procedure. Note: These qualified service provider manages the disposal of the bio-hazardous item(s). Note: The invoice should be paid on the claim file, under the existing cause of loss. |
 | the object is not embedded | go to the next step. |
2. Don latex gloves and use a tool, such as needle-nose pliers or tongs, to pick the article up.
3. Dispose of sharp objects in the sharp container, commonly located in the non-driveable vehicle estimating bay.
4. Clean the pliers or tongs with a bleach solution and rinse with water.

metadata.title: Handle and dispose of biohazardous materials
metadata.category: Occupational health and safety > Biohazard inspection and cleaning of a vehicle
metadata.description: Steps to handle and dispose of biohazardous materials in a vehicle.

text:
Note: For a bleach solution use 1 part bleach to 9 parts water.
5. Dispose of any items that have been in contact with blood/bodily fluids in a plastic bag.
6. Tie off the first plastic bag and place it in a second plastic bag. 

 Important: Keep the second bag open until you are finished with the gloves.
7. Carefully remove the latex gloves and drop them in the second plastic bag, tie off the bag and label it "Bio-Hazardous Material."

 Note: Bio-Hazardous Material labels are available from your first aid attendant.
8. Wash your hands with soap and water even if the gloves appear to be intact.
9. Call Occupational Health and Safety at 604-982-6315, when the sharp container is 3/4 full or bag(s) have been used

 Note: The cost of removal is paid by the claims office requesting the service.

 **Result:** 

 Occupational Health and Safety arranges for pick-up.

**Parent topic:** Biohazard inspection and cleaning of a vehicle

# Bio-hazard inspection and cleaning by qualified ICBC supplier

Guidelines for biohazard inspections and cleaning by qualified ICBC suppliers.

### Qualified supplier required

ICBC ensures all vehicles with an ICBC claim that are exposed to bio-hazardous materials are inspected and cleaned to reduce the exposure to our customers, staff and business partners.

If the vehicle may have been exposed to bio-hazardous materials it must be cleaned. The inspection and cleaning must be performed by a qualified ICBC supplier.

### When an area has no qualified supplier

For offices that do not have a qualified service provider the

* claim owner or estimator must explain to the customer that a risk of exposure to bio-hazardous materials may exist and the service is not available in their area, and
* decision to move the vehicle to a qualified service provider is the responsibility of the claims servicing office.

text:
### Avoiding bio-hazard exposure

Personal safety and appropriate consideration for the exposure to bio-hazard conditions is paramount. It may be necessary

* to vent the vehicle outdoors, and
* for people examining these vehicles to wear appropriate safety equipment (gloves, masks, etc.).

**Parent topic:** Biohazard inspection and cleaning of a vehicle

# Processing split windshield claims

The glass repair program participant creates or retrieves split windshield claims, when two glass panes are damaged at the same time.

### When this applies

When a customer has a claim for a split windshield, the participant identifies whether the damage resulted from one incident or multiple incidents.

**Example:** Damage to the second pane of glass may have occurred after the claim was opened by the claim centre.

This determines whether the customer has one claim with one deductible to be paid, or two claims with a deductible to be paid on each claim.

metadata.title: Processing split windshield claims
metadata.category: Glass > Procedures
metadata.description: The glass repair program participant creates or retrieves split windshield claims, when two glass panes are damaged at the same time.

text:
### Process

1. **Participant**
 1. Determines whether the two glass panes were damaged at the same time or in separate incidents.

 | When the two glass panes were ... | Then the participant ... |
 | --- | --- |
 | * not damaged at the same time, or * the customer has + two claim numbers, and + an ICBC Glass Claim Information (CL462C) form | * processes the two panes of the split windshield as two separate claims * uploads the digital images to the Vendor Document Image Application (VDIA), and * completes the claims. |
 | * damaged at the same time, or * the customer has + one claim number, and + a CL462C form | * processes the two panes of the split windshield as one claim * creates one claim in Glass Web Express (GWE) * uploads the digital images to VDIA, ensuring that close-up images of the damage to both windshield panes are included * contacts Provincial Glass Operations (PGO) to explain the reasons it is one claim, and * proceeds to stage 2. |

metadata.title: Processing split windshield claims
metadata.category: Glass > Procedures
metadata.description: The glass repair program participant creates or retrieves split windshield claims, when two glass panes are damaged at the same time.

text:
Note: There are two claims and two deductibles paid, when the
 * customer advises that both panes of glass were damaged at different times, or
 * investigation confirms the same conclusion.
2. **Provincial Glass Operations (PGO)**
 1. Reviews and confirms whether the damage is consistent with damage from one or two claims.

 | When PGO confirms damage to both panes is ... | Then the participant ... |
 | --- | --- |
 | one claim | * adds the second pane as an exception item, and * submits the Glass Replacement Invoice - (CL14BX) form and any supporting documentation and images to Vendor Document Image Application (VDIA). |
 | two separate claims with two deductibles | * creates a second claim * processes both claims, and * submits the Glass Replacement Invoice - (CL14BX) form and any supporting documentation and images to VDIA. |

**Parent topic:** Procedures

# Warranty on alternative parts

Summary of warranties on alternative part types.

### Warranty

The warranty on an alternative part depends upon the type of part utilized.

The warranty for each type of part is presented in the table.

| Type of part | Warranty |
| --- | --- |
| Aftermarket | Lifetime warranty for as long as the original owner owns the vehicle. |
| Alloy wheel | Lifetime warranty for as long as the original owner owns the vehicle. This applies to the following: * repaired wheels, and * recycled wheels. Note: The refinish application has a warranty of one year. |
| Exchange part | Lifetime warranty for as long as the original owner owns the vehicle. This applies to the following: * exchange bumpers * reinforcement bars, and * other exchange parts. |
| Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) surplus | one year. |
| radiators and air conditioning parts | Lifetime warranty for as long as the original owner owns the vehicle. |

metadata.title: Warranty on alternative parts
metadata.category: Repairs > Parts > Standards of performance on vehicle parts
metadata.description: Summary of warranties on alternative part types.

text:
### General limit of warranty

The parts supplier is not responsible for failure due to

* improper installation
* accident
* misuse
* abuse, or
* improper maintenance.

### Additional limits to warranty

The following specific limits apply over and above general warranty limits:

| Type of part | The parts supplier is not responsible for failure due to ... |
| --- | --- |
| Alloy wheel repair | wheel weights. |
| Exchange parts | * warping, other than premature warping, or * any subsequent repair or modification. |

### Failure during warranty period

Where a failure occurs to a part within the applicable warranty period, the parts supplier must

* replace the part, or
* refund the purchase price of that part to the repair facility that
 + purchased the part, or
 + replaced the defective partincluding
 + freight, and
 + all reasonable labour charges for removal and replacement, and where applicable, refinishing.

**Parent topic:** Standards of performance on vehicle parts

| Types of vehicle coverings | Features |
| --- | --- |
| Decal (full/partial/panel) | * Applied to either a single panel, multiple panels, or the full vehicle * Specified by the panel or vehicle * Can be removable, but are generally designed as permanent. |

# Water damage considerations

What to consider when determining the extent of water damage on a vehicle.

metadata.title: Water damage considerations
metadata.category: Repairs > Light duty estimates > Water damaged vehicle policy
metadata.description: What to consider when determining the extent of water damage on a vehicle.

text:
### Considerations and impacts

The table lists what to consider in a water damaged vehicle, which is information that will assist an estimator with determining if a vehicle is repairable or salvageable.

metadata.title: Water damage considerations
metadata.category: Repairs > Light duty estimates > Water damaged vehicle policy
metadata.description: What to consider when determining the extent of water damage on a vehicle.

text:
| Considerations | Details and impact |
| --- | --- |
| What are the circumstances of the water contact? | The circumstances of water contact can affect claim-related damage. Circumstances include * vehicle-to-water impact, and * rising water, such as due to flooding. |
| Was the water fresh water, sea water, or contaminated water? | Water may cause serious damage when water is * contaminated with + chemicals + petroleum products + fertilizers, or + other biological products, or * salt water. |
| Does the type of water impact anything? | Potential impacts of the type of water content, such as fresh water, sea water, or chemicals, includes * damage to upholstery * corrosion of metal in inaccessible areas of a vehicle, and * damage to electronic components and connections. |

metadata.title: Water damage considerations
metadata.category: Repairs > Light duty estimates > Water damaged vehicle policy
metadata.description: What to consider when determining the extent of water damage on a vehicle.

text:
| Was the motor vehicle immersing or traversing? | A vehicle that * was immersed, refers to a complete or partial submersion of a vehicle, and the results are almost certain water seepage and damage, and * had been traversed, refers to a vehicle being driven + through low levels of water, and + where no hazards were present. Note: The vehicle should be carefully examined, if water seepage or damage is suspected. Note: Most vehicles are intended to be driven through shallow water, and can lead long and productive service lives in wet climates. |
| What was the depth of immersion? | A vehicle is considered flood-damaged when it is or has been immersed in a liquid to * the bottom of the dashboard, or * a level affecting any of the vehicle's major electrical system components. Note: For additional information, refer to the topic, Flood damaged vehicle policy.") |

metadata.title: Water damage considerations
metadata.category: Repairs > Light duty estimates > Water damaged vehicle policy
metadata.description: What to consider when determining the extent of water damage on a vehicle.

text:
| What is the length of time between recovery and the estimate or repairs? | The longer it takes to estimate and assess the vehicle damage, the greater the likelihood the water and its contaminants will migrate into the vehicle components and assemblies. This could result in contaminated * lubricants * upholstery, and * compromised safety and electrical components. |
| Was the vehicle's motor running at the time of immersion? | If enough water is introduced such as when the vehicle is immersed, or it impacts the water surface, water can be sucked into the engine and cause immediate damage to expensive internal components of the engine. |
| Was there additional damage resulting from the vehicle's recovery or extraction? | Recovery or extraction of a vehicle can create further claim-related damage to the * suspension * running gear, and * vehicle structure. Water in the vehicle may enter into previously undamaged areas when the vehicle is raised or is in transit. |

# Settle total loss with endorsement

Steps to settle a total loss vehicle with an endorsement.

### When this applies

When a total loss occurs to a vehicle with an endorsement, the customer is entitled to additional compensation with their total loss settlement.

metadata.title: Settle total loss with endorsement
metadata.category: Total losses and salvage
metadata.description: Steps to settle a total loss vehicle with an endorsement.

text:
### Procedure

1. Establish the net purchase price.

 * obtain a copy of the purchase agreement, and
 * consider any equipment added to the vehicle according to applicable regulations and acts, and
 * if the vehicle was purchased used and a replacement vehicle is not available within 30 days, then refer to the Autoplan Optional Policy, Division 9 Special Coverage Terms and Conditions.
2. Complete the applicable worksheet.

 | If the customer has this endorsement... | Then use this worksheet... |
 | --- | --- |
 | Replacement Cost (APV286A) | Replacement Cost Policy Worksheet (CL30J). |
 | New Vehicle Replacement (NVR+) | Replacement Cost Policy Worksheet (CL30J). |
 | Limited Depreciation (APV297A) | Limited Depreciation Worksheet (CL30F). |

 Note: Should the customer wish to delay settlement longer than 30 days for the replacement of the same vehicle, this can be extended to 90 days.

metadata.category: Total losses and salvage
metadata.description: Steps to settle a total loss vehicle with an endorsement.

 * the decision of which settlement to accept is up to the lessor, not the lessee, and

# Battery disconnection policy

Any damaged vehicle that poses a fire or explosion risk must have the battery cables disconnected at the source, when the vehicle is stored inside a claims servicing office outside of normal operating hours, or being dispatched to an ICBC salvage facility.

### Applicability

This applies to all vehicle; including, electric hybrid vehicles.

Note: The Estimating Service Manager is responsible to ensure compliance with this policy.

### Exceptions

The battery does not need to be disconnected when the severity of the damage

* prevents access to the battery, or
* results in safety concerns.

**Parent topic:** Safety considerations

# Environmental handling charges and electronic handling fees

Definitions for environmental handling charges and electronic handling fees.

Environmental handling charges are charges that the supplier must pay for the purchase of specified products related to the customer’s vehicle repairs. These fees are:

* paid to the retailer
* charged at the point of purchase, and
* reflects the cost of recycling the purchased item.

Suppliers must pay environment handling charges on Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) supplied equipment.

### Electronic handling fees

Electronic handling fees are fees that the supplier must pay for the purchaser of specified products related to the customer’s vehicle repairs. These fees are:

* paid to the retailer
* charged at the point of purchase, and
* reflects the cost of recycling the purchased item.

Suppliers are not required to pay electronic fees on OEM supplied electronic equipment.

# Calculate the co-insurance amount for a declared value vehicle

Steps on calculating the co-insurance amount for a declared value vehicle.

### Prerequisites

ClaimCenter has automatically indicated on a claim's co-insurance tab that a declared value policy is in effect.

### When this applies

When a declared value policy is in effect, and the value appears inaccurate against the described vehicle, an estimator or appraiser must determine whether co-insurance applies. When it does, the customer and repair facility are advised of any co-insurance, if applicable.

The estimator or appraiser must use the co-insurance calculator to determine applicable co-insurance

* percentage amount before starting repairs, and
* dollar amount after repairs are completed.

Note: Co-insurance only applies to a customer accessing their Own Damage coverage, and not on claims where Basic Vehicle Damage coverage is being accessed.

metadata.title: Calculate the co-insurance amount for a declared value vehicle
metadata.category: Vehicle damage > Estimates > Complete a commercial estimate for a non-network repair facility
metadata.description: Steps on calculating the co-insurance amount for a declared value vehicle.

text:
### Procedure

1. Review the declared value amount against the vehicle.

 Note: For calculating the declared value, refer to the topic, Co-insurance calculation.

 | If the declared value ... | Then ... |
 | --- | --- |
 | appears accurate | the co-insurance calculator is not required. |
 | does not appear accurate | * establish the actual cash value (ACV) * add the ACV amount in the co-insurance calculator, and * proceed to step 2. |
2. Update the claim by

 * adding the total cost of repairs into the co-insurance calculator
 * adding the deductible amount, if applicable, and
 * updating the co-insurance calculator.
3. Provide the customer and repair facility, the percentage and dollar amounts of co-insurance the customer is responsible for on the claim, after the vehicle repairs are completed.
4. Add a note to the claim, documenting the information provided to the customer and the repair facility.

**Parent topic:** Complete a commercial estimate for a non-network repair facility

When a customer applies for reimbursement and/or replacement of a child car seat, the exposure owner determines if the customer is eligible for full reimbursement, or a set amount, using the Child car seat reimbursement types and eligibility policy.

ICBC provides a guide to customers on icbc.com for the

* child car seat types that are available, and
* manufacturer's age and height/weight requirements associated with each child car seat.

Important: This is a guide only. A customer must use a child car seat in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions and British Columbia (B.C) legislation, which are both the ultimate authority on child car seat requirements.

A description for each child car seat type is provided in the table.

# Tow dispatch

Definition of a tow dispatch by ICBC.

A tow dispatch is a request for a continuous tow from the vehicle location to a specified destination.

When the vehicle arrives at the specified destination and the repair facility requests it not to be unloaded, then the tow company may choose to return and unload the vehicle at their storage facility (yard and/or building).

Appropriate towing and storage charges will apply when the vehicle is taken back to a storage facility (yard and/or building). ICBC must be updated of any destination tow changes by the tow facility.

Note: It is at the discretion of the tow company to deliver the vehicle to a second destination, when the repair facility changes the original drop off destination.

metadata.title: Tow dispatch
metadata.category: Non-drivable vehicles and tows > Towing > Storage
metadata.description: Definition of a tow dispatch by ICBC.

# Sale of salvage to qualified organizations policy

Salvage vehicles can be sold or loaned to qualified organizations through requests made to the manager of Salvage Operations in the requesting area. Organizations that have vehicles loaned to them are responsible for the towing the vehicle from the salvage facility and returning the vehicle to the facility.

metadata.title: Sale of salvage to qualified organizations policy
metadata.category: Total losses and salvage > Salvage > Rules on owner buy back of salvage
metadata.description: Salvage vehicles can be sold or loaned to qualified organizations through requests made to the manager of Salvage Operations in the requesting area. Organizations that have vehicles loaned to them are responsible for the towing the vehicle from the salvage facility and returning the vehicle to the facility.

### Qualified organizations

| Qualified organization | Requirements |
| --- | --- |
| * Trade schools * Colleges * Educational organizations | Vehicles can be sold through normal bid auctions for educational purposes only, upon qualification by Salvage Operations. Note: Salvage vehicles cannot be loaned to educational institutions. |
| Fire, police, and emergency services | Vehicles with little to no salvage value can be loaned under the external loan agreement. |
| Research organizations, such as * UBC, or * Pacific Traffic Educator Centre (PTEC) | Vehicles can be sold or loaned to these organizations for research purposes. |

Important: Salvage vehicles cannot be donated.

.

# Salvage overview

Policy on processing salvage through Salvage Operations.

metadata.title: Salvage overview
metadata.category: Total losses and salvage > Salvage
metadata.description: Policy on processing salvage through Salvage Operations.

text:
### Policy detail on salvage assets, vehicle disposal and use of ICBC facilities

When ICBC replaces or pays the declared or actual cash value (ACV) for a vehicle or its equipment, the salvage becomes the property of ICBC. All salvage is considered to have a cash recovery value.

All salvage assets must

* be processed and authorized through Salvage Operations, and
* not be disposed of without the authorization of either the salvage manager or designate.

Note: Claims staff and independent adjusters are not permitted to dispose of salvage without the approval of either the salvage manager or their designate.

ICBC employees and members of their immediate family are not permitted to purchase any salvage, either directly or indirectly through a

* friend
* acquaintance
* family member, or
* other proxy.

ICBC facilities must not be used for

* rebuilding vehicles for sale
* servicing of vehicles for personal use or gain, or
* repairing personal vehicle or otherwise personal gain.

# Compensation for labour on recycled parts

Summary of recycled parts that are compensated for labour.

When a recycled parts supplier provides a part that requires repairing or refurbishing, then compensation for labour must be

* fair and mutually agreeable by repair facility and the recycled parts supplier, and
* paid by the recycled part supplier before the part is installed.

### Exceptions

ICBC may approve compensation for labour when:

* recycled part is returned for reasons beyond the recycler’s control, and
* custom cutting of sheet metal recycled parts on a vehicle reduces or eliminates the opportunity for resale.

### Example

Estimator determines the vehicle is repairable, but while it is being repaired it is discovered there is additional hidden damage. The additional hidden damage may cause:

* repairs dollar amount to increase, and
* vehicle becomes a total loss.

**Parent topic:** Recycled parts requirements

ICBC pays the claim required tows, additional services charged, and vehicle storage days for the dispatched vehicle.

text:
### Applicability

Note: ICBC does not pay for tow or storage related to police holds or impounds.

When tow suppliers receive either an ICBC external tow dispatch, or a photo or invoice request for vehicles in their storage facility, such as a yard and/or building, they agree to

* release the dispatched vehicle, if the vehicle needs to be towed
* send the photos provided in the request, and
* invoice ICBC for all vehicle claim required
 + tows and distance charges
 + additional service charges, and
 + vehicle claim required and/or applicable salvage required storage days.

ICBC pays tow suppliers for dispatched and/or invoices requested for vehicles in accordance to the Towing Storage Rate Payment Schedule (CL332) form, and the Claims Procedures manual.

Note: ICBC does not consider the payment of a vehicle tow between storage facilities and/or buildings that are owned, leased or shared, that is not dispatched by ICBC.

# Requirements for towing a vehicle to a storage facility

Policy on claim eligibility, rates, supplier responsibilities, and the conditions for requesting a tow.

### Policy

ICBC pays for claim required tows, additional services, and storage days in accordance with the Towing and Storage Rate Payment Schedule (CL332) and Material Damage procedures. By accepting a Tow Dispatch Request, suppliers agree to bill ICBC in accordance with the Schedule and Procedures, and to release the vehicle(s) to ICBC, as and when directed by ICBC.

### Non-ICBC dispatched tows

ICBC may not consider the payment of a vehicle tow between storage compounds and/or buildings, either owned, leased or shared, that is not dispatched by ICBC. For example, if at the scene of an accident the police direct the tow driver to tow the vehicle to a compound lot, ICBC does not pay the tow charge.

metadata.category: Non-drivable vehicles and tows > Towing > Storage
metadata.description: Policy on claim eligibility, rates, supplier responsibilities, and the conditions for requesting a tow.

### Tow supplier responsibilities

When a tow supplier accepts a Tow Dispatch or Photo Triage Request or Direct Payment Invoicing they

* agree to release the vehicle, and
* invoice ICBC in accordance with the applicable Towing and Storage Rate Payment Schedule (CL322) form for all claims that require

 + tows and distance charges,
 + additional service charges, and
 + storage days.

metadata.category: Non-drivable vehicles and tows > Towing > Storage
metadata.description: Policy on claim eligibility, rates, supplier responsibilities, and the conditions for requesting a tow.

text:
### Eligible claims

ICBC pays towing and storage for a claim

* that has ICBC Basic Vehicle Damage coverage, if ICBC authorizes and dispatches a tow, or requests an invoice
* with ICBC Own Damage coverage for the cause of loss, if ICBC has authorized the claim, or
* involving a Combination Vehicle incident, when
 + the customer has ICBC Own Damage coverage, for the damaged vehicle, and
 + the claims representative has authorized the claim for one or more of the combination of vehicles, or
 + the claim is under investigation.

Note: In a combination vehicle incident, ICBC pays first tow expenses for attached vehicles that are undamaged, such as a trailer.

metadata.title: Requirements for towing a vehicle to a storage facility
metadata.category: Non-drivable vehicles and tows > Towing > Storage
metadata.description: Policy on claim eligibility, rates, supplier responsibilities, and the conditions for requesting a tow.

text:
### Conditions for a tow dispatch

ICBC dispatches vehicles or contacts a tow company for any of these conditions

* there is an insurable interest in the vehicle
* there is an authorized ICBC claim with Own Damage or Basic Vehicle Damage coverages
* the vehicle is required to be moved from one location to another, or
* ICBC is requesting an invoice from a tow supplier.

### Tow rates

Claim required, first tows, from the initial vehicle recovery location to a storage yard and/or building, including total theft recovered vehicles, are paid by the First Tow rate on each vehicle on the claim with the Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) category.

Claim required, second or additional tows, are paid by the Claim Required Second & Additional Tow rate by GVWR category.

Towing and storage costs are based on the account/facility number attached to the storage yard/building closest to where the vehicle was originally recovered.

**Parent topic:** Storage

Information regarding non-captive tow rotations lists.

Non-captive tows are distributed by a claim centre or ICBC Salvage facility.

| an ICBC Salvage facility | distributed in order of rotation list: * based on the percentage of the individual tow company's vehicle count, and * which tow company's facilities have main storage facilities within 30 km from an ICBC Salvage facility. |

The Estimate or Appraisal uses several terms to describe specific repair or replace related items.

| Like Kind (LK) | Parts from a donor vehicle supplied by an auto recycler (auto wrecker). |
| Sublet | A dollar amount for a service not normally performed by the repair facility. Examples: * a wheel alignment, which is done at a mechanical facility * interior cleaning * custom graphics * lock recoding Note: Prices for each of these would be in the sublet column of the Estimate or Appraisal. |
| Repair Hours (RP) | The amount of time it takes to repair a panel or part on a vehicle. |
| Remove/Replace (RR) Hours | The amount of time it takes to remove the old part and replace it. |

# Obtain a signed Vehicle Ownership Transfer Agreement

Obtain a signed Vehicle Ownership Transfer Agreement (CL96), which includes a verbal, from the registered owner (RO) or multiple ROs to transfer ownership of the vehicle to ICBC.

### Prerequisites

The claim does not have vehicle estimate holds and is not a heavy equipment vehicle claim.

Note: For vehicle types in commercial claims, refer to Obtain a signed Commercial Write-off Agreement (CL96L) form and release the vehicle for sale.").

### When this applies

A CL96 is required when ICBC expects the customer's vehicle will be a total loss.

The CL96 is requested when

* the TLP Result displays "Obvious Total Loss" or "Possible Total Loss", or
* the estimator completes their tasks to Confirm a total loss.

metadata.category: Total losses and salvage > Salvage

### Procedure

1. Advise the RO of the total loss status.

 Important: The customer signing the CL96 form must be the RO on the policy. In addition, each RO must sign their own CL96 form.

 1. Contact the customer and ask the ICBC customer verification questions.
 2. Confirm the customer's email address, if available.
 3. Tell the customer what the possible total loss result means:

 * "Based on what you have shared with ICBC to date, it looks like your vehicle may not be repairable."
 * "The repair facility or ICBC will inspect your vehicle, then we will determine if it can be repaired or not."
 * "If ICBC determines that your vehicle cannot be repaired, we will begin the salvage process, meaning that it will either be sold or disposed of. ICBC will determine the amount you are entitled to under your policy and pay that out to you."

# Owner retention and owner buy back comparison

Comparison of an owner retention and an owner buy back of a total loss vehicle for salvage or dismantle purposes.

### Owner retention

An owner retention is when the owner of a vehicle chooses to retain the total loss vehicle for salvage or dismantle purposes.

The owner must sign and submit an Owner Retention Agreement (CL96C or CL96M) form.

Note: To view examples of total loss agreements, refer to Total Loss Salvage and Owner Retention Agreements.

The salvage value amount payable by the customer, known as the salvage deduction, does not include taxes, as the vehicle is being retained rather than sold.

metadata.title: Owner retention and owner buy back comparison
metadata.category: Total losses and salvage > Salvage > Rules on owner retention of salvage
metadata.description: Comparison of an owner retention and an owner buy back of a total loss vehicle for salvage or dismantle purposes.

text:
### Owner buy back

An owner buy back is when a Beneficial owner or Lessee wants to purchase their total loss vehicle, in which multiple owners are involved, for salvage or dismantle purposes.

A Vehicle Ownership Transfer Agreement (CL96) form must be signed by the registered owner, and a Salvage Purchase Agreement (CL96D or CL96N) form must be signed by the intended purchaser.

The salvage value amount payable by the purchaser, known as the salvage deduction, includes applicable taxes.

Actual Cash Value (ACV) is inclusive of applicable tax allowances.

**Parent topic:** Rules on owner retention of salvage

# Failed windshield repair

The glass repair program participant works with Provincial Glass Operations (PGO) when handling a failed windshield repair. A windshield repair failure occurs when a previously repaired chip or crack has spread beyond its original repaired state.

text:
### Policy

When a windshield repair failure occurs,

* ICBC advises the customer to return to the glass repair program facility that completed the original windshield repair as identified on the previously paid Windshield Repair Invoice (CL14BXR)
* the participant must contact PGO to confirm the failed windshield repair, and
* PGO must associate the current windshield claim with the previous paid windshield repair claim.

Note: The windshield repair allowance will be deducted from the cost of the replacement when the failed repair is replaced at the same facility that performed the original repair.

The windshield repair allowance is deducted from the gross total of the windshield replacement costs upon PGO confirmation of a failed windshield repair.

# Pre-repair and post-repair scanning policy

Overview of pre-repair and post-repair diagnostic scanning, including the use of Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) scanning.

metadata.title: Pre-repair and post-repair scanning policy
metadata.category: Repairs > Light duty estimates > Estimating technical
metadata.description: Overview of pre-repair and post-repair diagnostic scanning, including the use of Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) scanning.

text:
### Policy

Pre-repair and post-repair diagnostic scanning operations involve inserting a scanning and diagnostic tool into an on-board diagnostics (OBD) II port and following the tool prompts to generate a scan report.

Note: For Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) pre-repair and post-repair scanning, an OEM scanning and diagnostic tool is used.

A pre-repair scan is performed prior to tear down, while a post-repair scan is performed following a repair. These scans assist in discovery and clearing of any specific Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTC’s).

ADAS calibration and/or in depth diagnostic analysis or diagnosis is not included in the pre and post repair scanning policy.

ICBC recognizes that pre-repair and post-repair scans may be warranted in the following categories.

metadata.category: Repairs > Light duty estimates > Estimating technical
metadata.description: Overview of pre-repair and post-repair diagnostic scanning, including the use of Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) scanning.

text:
| Category | Requirements |
| --- | --- |
| Vehicle year 2011 and newer | Vehicles 2011 or newer, do not require Needs Attention from the Mitchell Compliance Utility for the following scenarios: **Pre-repair scan:** * MIL (Malfunction Indicator Light) present. **Example**: Supplemental Restraint System (SRS), Electronic Stability Control (ESC), Check engine * mechanical damage, which may generate a code, such as suspension, stability control, or possible catastrophic engine failure * non-driveable vehicle * claims where hidden damage impacts ADAS functionality * recovered/attempted theft, and * rodent damage claims. **Important**: If the vehicle is potentially a total loss, pre-repair scans may be warranted. **Post-repair scan:** Permitted on all vehicles 2011 and newer. |

metadata.category: Repairs > Light duty estimates > Estimating technical

text:
### Documentation

Scanning results are kept on file in accordance with the documentation requirements of the Collision Repair Program Guide.

### Allowance

Pre-repair and/or post-repair scans are paid an allowance of 0.3 hours at the current applicable body rate based on the vendor status. To perform this in Mitchell Cloud Estimating (MCE), add the following My Templates repair lines: ICBC PRE REPAIR SCAN or ICBC POST SCAN.

For repair participants using OEM scan tools with a certified red seal mechanic on site, the pre-repair and post-repair scans must be

* manually entered as OEM SCAN REQUIRED in the MCE system
* paid at an allowance of 0.5 hours in lieu of both pre-repair and post-repair scan using the ICBC mechanical labour operation, and
* manually entered for 0.5 hours calculated at the door rate for the mechanical rate differential.

Note: The door rate is the posted dealer mechanical rate.

Instances where an aftermarket scan tool is not sufficient, and a factory scan tool, OEM or equivalent (Astech/Airpro) is required, Needs Attention must be selected for approval, via the Mitchell Estimating system.

Note: Pre and post-repair scan allowance is paid per scan operation performed by the repair participant. In certain instances, more than one pre or post-repair scan may be required.

# Vehicle rental rates policy

ICBC will authorize only preferred rates except where the exposure owner has deemed a different rate as reasonable under the circumstances.

### Policy

Unless there is a note with the Topic of "Rental Vehicle" on the claim, the claims admin (LOU team) can only authorize the rate for a similar-sized vehicle, as outlined in the ICBC rental rate structure and as offered by preferred rental vehicle providers.

### Loss of Use coverage

In LOU scenarios, ICBC can specify the make and model of available substitute vehicle when providing alternate transportation to a customer. The expense incurred for the alternate transportation cannot exceed either the per-day limit or the total limit of the coverage purchased by the insured and described in the insured's owner's certificate.

If the customer wants to rent a more expensive vehicle, the LOU representative must confirm with the exposure owner. Otherwise, the customer must pay the difference in price.

# When to assign an accountant or economist

Policy on when it is appropriate to assign a financial professional from the approved lists of accountants and economists.

### Policy

Claims representatives who require financial loss investigation support, must determine if a claim is eligible to be assigned to a financial professional from the approved lists of accountants and economists, before the assignment can be requested.

If defence counsel (DC) determines a financial investigation expert is required, they must review it with the claims representative before taking action. For a claims representative and/or DC to retain an accounting firm or economists firm for a claim, they must refer to ICBC's approved list of firms available in Accountants and Economists, and select one of those firms.

Services are retained through standard communication methods, such as phone, email, or letter, and providing documentation for review.

### Eligibility

Some indications that a claim would make a good candidate for a financial loss investigation include

* a customer (plaintiff) is a
 + semi-professional
 + business owner
 + high income earner
 + self-employed earner
 + commission sales earner, and/or
 + contractor or side venture earner, and/or
* flags on the claim that prompt the need for assistance, such as
 + a wage loss that is difficult to calculate
 + a fraud or Special Investigation Unit (SIU) flag, or
 + other red flag.

text:
### Policy

When adjusters request assignment of a financial professional (financial partner) in the FPP, they must determine the phase of the FPP that is appropriate for the file to be allocated to, in accordance with:

* this policy
* Policy on assigning a financial professional in the Financial Partners Program, and
* the procedure, Financial Partners Program overview for exsiting Financial Partners Program assignments.

Financial loss claims that need to be allocated to:

* Phase 1, are not applicable as this is for the completion of the discontinued Economic Loss Assignment (CL472) (web) form only
* Phases 2, 4 or 5:
 + do not require approval when the phase allocation is determined by an claims specialist, or
 + require manager approval when the phase allocation is determined by an adjuster, and
* Phase 3, requires:
 + approval from the adjuster's manager, and
 + completion of Phase 2 prior to allocation to Phase 3.

text:
### Procedure

1. Prepare written instructions for the financial professional. 

 Note: When a claim is litigated, the claims representative should seek input from defence counsel (DC).
2. Determine file material required by the financial professional.
3. Determine if you need to authorize the assigned financial professional to send a letter to the 

 * customer (plaintiff), and/or
 * plaintiff counsel (PC).

 Important: This letter is at the discretion of the claims representative and is not required. The assigned financial professional can only send this letter when the claims representative has provided approval to proceed. If the letter is sent, it should
 * advise the plaintiff or PC of the financial professionals involvement in the claim, and
 * request the required documents needed to conduct the financial loss investigation.

 * discuss the work required for the file, based on

# Rates for preferred rental vehicles

The claims representative should encourage customers to use the preferred rental vehicle provider at a location; however customers always have the choice.

### Rental vehicle rates for preferred suppliers

Most locations in B.C. have a preferred rental vehicle provider who has an agreement with ICBC to offer advantageous rates, benefits, and services in exchange for ICBC marketing their service to customers.

In most cases, the rates from the preferred provider for a location will be the best available to the customer, relative to the rental rates of non-preferred suppliers in that location. Even where it is not, the ICBC representative should encourage the customer to use the preferred supplier.

Rental vehicle rates in general depend on

* the region, and
* the vehicle class.

Rates for Rental vehicles are also available on our website.

# Request a tow

Claims support assistants (CSA) may request a vehicle tow from a tow company.

### When this applies

When a request to tow a vehicle has been received by the claims support assistant. Tow requests can be made by

* phoning the tow company, or
* completing and sending via email or fax, an External Tow Dispatch Request (CL602) form.

The following information should be provided, regardless of method

* claim number
* vehicle's year, make or model
* current location of vehicle
* current location of the vehicle's keys, if available
* number of sets of keys
* location that the vehicle should be towed to, and
* condition of vehicle, such as missing tires, or fire damage.

### Procedure

1. Contact the tow company via desired method.
2. Add an entry in the Vehicle Incident screen in ClaimCenter, providing the tow request details.

 Note: Refer to the ClaimCenter user guide topic, Add the vehicle location, for information on how to add the entry in ClaimCenter.

# Requirements for sublet towing service billing

List of requirements for sublet towing services invoices.

### Requirements

When a sublet towing company has been used, the original tow company must attach a copy of the company’s invoice to the Towing Invoice (CL14C) form that they submit to ICBC.

A sublet towing company’s invoice must include the following:

* company name
* number of employees
* retail charge out rate
* trade discount, if any
* length of time at the motor vehicle crash location
* arrival and departure times
* travel time
* distance travelled
* signature
* date, and
* explanations or photos documenting reasons for the sublet charges.

| * Non-urgent, and * ICBC does not handle the direct billing of the sublet services or equipment. | Tow company: * arranges the required services or rental equipment, and * applies the 15% markup to the invoiced net sublet amount charges,subject to the trade discount policy. |

# Supplier Conduct Committee

Overview of the Supplier Conduct Committee

### Definition

The Supplier Conduct Committee reviews suppliers who create reputational or financial risk for ICBC due to not following claims procedures, performance standards or contractual obligations to the corporation.

The Supplier Conduct Committee’s mandate is to:

* provide guidance on all supplier conduct issues
* protect the safety of customers and eliminate risk
* offer consistency on supplier conduct
* recommend the disciplinary steps, and
* identify personnel responsible for implementation of said discipline.

The committee is comprised of:

| Voting committee members | * Director, Claims Customer and MD Strategy * Director, Claims Programs and Strategy * Director, Claims Operations, or * Director, Claims Services. |
| Supporting committee members | * Lawyer, Corporate Law * Advisor, Issues Management * Advisor, Stakeholder Relations * Manager, Supplier Management Office * Manager/Advisor, Supplier Performance Management (presenting ), or * Coordinator, Supplier Programs (minutes). |

text:
### Tasks

The Supplier Conduct Committee addresses matters relating to a supplier’s conduct, and determines appropriate disciplinary action assessing:

* intent
* frequency
* severity, and
* impact of compliance or conduct.

It also provides guidance on a variety of issues, such as:

* unsatisfactory and/or unsafe repairs
* billing and invoicing issues
* unauthorized changes to the Estimate/Appraisal form
* non-compliance with claims procedures, supplier programs, performance standards, and/or agreements, and
* business practices of:
 + MD
 + Health Services, and
 + investigative partners.

# Trade discounts on sublet services

Overview of trade discounts on sublet services.

### Trade discounts

When assistance from a sublet company is required or additional equipment with a posted retail rate is rented, then the:

* expectation ICBC puts on the original tow company is to attempt to obtain a trade discount on the service and equipment cost, and
* trade discount must be obtained through a business to business negotiation.

Important: Occasionally, a tow company is unable to negotiate any trade discount percentage on the cost of the service or equipment required. Billing is allowed at the applicable markup percentage (up to 15%) over net payment

# Vehicle disposition notification

Information regarding the use of the Vehicle Disposition Notification (APV377) form.

### Vehicle disposition notification form

ICBC has agreed to, in alignment with Canadian Council Motor Transport Authority (CCMTA) guidelines, report any out-of-province vehicles considered a total loss to the issuing jurisdiction’s vehicle registry.

A Vehicle Disposition Notification (APV377) form must be completed to contact an out of province vehicle registry, when a vehicle registered outside of BC is involved in a crash with a responsible ICBC insured vehicle operating outside BC, and is determined to be a total loss.

The out of province vehicle can be from:

* another Canadian province or territory, or
* an American state.

Note: ICBC contacts the issuing registry as long as the vehicle meets salvage designation criteria, even if a cash settlement has paid on the total loss.

**Parent topic:** Out of province support

# Markup charge

Definition of a markup charge relating to sublet towing services

### Definition

A markup charge is a percentage, up to 15%, applied to sublet towing services. Markup charges are

* allowed only on services completed by a company or employee other than the towing company originally called to the crash location, and
* calculated on the net amount of the invoice provided by the sublet provider.

### Use

The markup percentage is intended to cover

* administration costs for contacting and arranging services or additional equipment
* advance payment for the cost of equipment or services
* account management and billing fees, and
* financial risks associated with collections.

### Exception of use

The markup costs are not applied when a trade discount has been provided.

# WorkCenter Total Loss Valuation Report

The WorkCenter Total Loss Valuation Report is an independent valuation service provided to ICBC by Mitchell. It comprises a comprehensive database which is updated weekly using data gathered from multiple sources. The WorkCenter Total Loss Valuation Report is the primary source for determining actual cash value (ACV) for vehicles.

### Use of the WorkCenter Total Loss Valuation Report

All actual cash value (ACV) valuations must be completed using the WorkCenter Total Loss Valuation Report. When WorkCenter Total Loss Valuation Report cannot complete the requested valuation, then a manual ACV should be completed.

Note: Refer to Actual cash value policy to the registered owner (RO) in the form of a total loss settlement.") for more information.
